title.zh: 卷八十八 列傳第十三 劉斐
title.raw: 卷八十八 列傳第十三 劉斐 Volume 88 Biographies 13: Liu Fei

sentences.zh: 劉文靜字肇仁，自言系出彭城，世居京兆武功。

translations.literal: Liu Wenjing, courtesy name Zhaoren, himself said his lineage issued from Pengcheng, and his family for generations dwelt in Jingzhao, Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenjing, courtesy name Zhaoren, claimed descent from Pengcheng; his family had long resided in Wugong, in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父韶，仕隋戰死，贈上儀同三司。

translations.literal: His father Shao served the Sui, died in battle, and was posthumously granted Senior Privy Counselor of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shao served the Sui dynasty, fell in battle, and was posthumously granted the title of Senior Privy Counselor of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 文靜以死難子式，藝術家是高度擴張自我、表現自我的人。

translations.literal: Wenjing, as the son of one who had died in loyal service, inherited the rank of Yitong.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of a man who had died in loyal service, Wenjing inherited the rank of Yitong.

sentences.zh: 主要著作有，襲儀同。

translations.literal: He inherited the rank of Yitong.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the rank of Yitong.

sentences.zh: 侗儻有器略。

translations.literal: Unrestrained and bold, he possessed strategic capacity.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and unconventional, with genuine talent for strategy.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為晉陽令，與晉陽宮監裴寂善。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign, he served as magistrate of Jinyang and was on good terms with Pei Ji, overseer of the Jinyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye era he served as magistrate of Jinyang and was on friendly terms with Pei Ji, overseer of the Jinyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 寂夜見邏堞傳烽，咤曰：「天下方亂，吾將安舍？

translations.literal: One night Ji saw beacon fires relayed along the patrol battlements and exclaimed: "The realm is just now in turmoil—where shall I take shelter?
translations.idiomatic: One night Ji saw beacon fires flashing along the battlements and cried out, "The empire is falling into chaos—where am I to find refuge?

sentences.zh: 」文靜笑曰：「如君言，豪英所資也。

translations.literal: " Wenjing laughed and said: "As you put it, this is exactly what heroes rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenjing laughed and said, "If that is so, then this is precisely what a great man needs.

sentences.zh: 吾二人者可終 賤乎？」

translations.literal: Can the two of us end our days in low station?"
translations.idiomatic: Can the two of us spend our lives in obscurity?"

sentences.zh: 高祖為唐公，鎮太原，文靜察有大誌，深自結。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Duke of Tang and stationed at Taiyuan, Wenjing perceived that he harbored great ambition and attached himself deeply to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu was still Duke of Tang and held Taiyuan, Wenjing saw that he harbored great ambition and cultivated a close bond with him.

sentences.zh: 既又見秦王，謂寂曰：「唐公子，非常人也，豁達神武，漢高祖、魏太祖之徒歟！

translations.literal: Later he also met the Prince of Qin and said to Ji: "The Duke of Tang's son is no ordinary man—open-minded and divinely martial; is he not of the sort of Han Gaozu and Wei Taizu?
translations.idiomatic: He later met the Prince of Qin as well and told Ji, "The Duke of Tang's son is no ordinary man—magnanimous and martially gifted. Is he not in the line of Han Gaozu and Wei Taizu?

sentences.zh: 殆天啟之也。

translations.literal: Perhaps Heaven has opened the way for him.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps Heaven itself has opened the way for him.

sentences.zh: 」寂未謂然。

translations.literal: " Ji did not yet agree.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji was not yet persuaded.

sentences.zh: 文靜俄坐李密姻屬系獄，秦王顧它無可與計者，私入視之。

translations.literal: Before long Wenjing was imprisoned on account of marriage ties to Li Mi; the Prince of Qin, looking about and finding no one else with whom to plan, entered secretly to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wenjing was imprisoned because of his marriage connection to Li Mi. The Prince of Qin, finding no one else with whom he could consult, entered the prison in secret to see him.

sentences.zh: 文靜喜，挑言曰：「喪亂方剡，非湯、武、高、光不能定。

translations.literal: Wenjing was delighted and provoked him, saying: "Ruin and chaos are now at their sharpest—only a Tang or Wu, a Gaozu or Guangwu, can bring order.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing was overjoyed and tested him, saying, "The age of ruin and chaos has reached its crisis. Only a Tang or Wu, a Gaozu or Guangwu, can restore order.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「安知無其人哉？

translations.literal: " The prince said: "How do you know there is no such man?
translations.idiomatic: " The prince said, "Who is to say that no such man exists?

sentences.zh: 今過此，非兒女子姁姁相憂者。

translations.literal: To pass this by now is not what girls chattering in mutual worry would do.
translations.idiomatic: To let this moment pass is not the way of women fretting among themselves.

sentences.zh: 世道將革，直欲共大計，試為我言之。

translations.literal: The age is about to change; I wish directly to share in a great design—try telling me what you think.
translations.idiomatic: The world is about to turn. I mean to join in a great design—tell me what you propose.

sentences.zh: 」文靜曰：「上南幸，兵填河、洛，盜賊蜉結，大連州縣，小阻山澤，以萬數，須真主取而用之。

translations.literal: " Wenjing said: "The emperor has gone south on tour; soldiers fill the Yellow and Luo rivers; bandits swarm like mayflies—large bands linking prefectures and counties, small ones blocking mountains and marshes—they number in the tens of thousands and await a true lord to take and employ them.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenjing said, "The emperor has gone south on tour. Armies choke the Yellow and Luo rivers. Bandits swarm everywhere—large bands linking whole prefectures and counties, smaller bands holding the hills and marshes. They number in the tens of thousands, waiting for a true ruler to gather and deploy them.

sentences.zh: 誠能投天會機，奮礻藝大呼，則四海不足定也。

translations.literal: If one can truly seize Heaven's opening and the moment's opportunity, raise one's sleeves and cry out, then the four seas would not be difficult to settle.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly seize Heaven's appointed moment, raise your sleeves and cry out to the realm, then even the four seas would not be hard to pacify.

sentences.zh: 今汾、晉避盜者皆在，文靜素知其豪傑，一朝號召，十萬眾可得也。

translations.literal: Now those fleeing bandits from Fen and Jin are all gathered here; Wenjing has long known the region's heroes—call them with a single proclamation and a hundred thousand men can be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Those fleeing the turmoil in Fen and Jin are all here now. Wenjing has long known the local heroes; with one call to arms, a hundred thousand men could be raised.

sentences.zh: 加公府兵數萬，一下令，誰不願從？

translations.literal: Add the ducal office troops numbering tens of thousands—as soon as you give the order, who would not wish to follow?
translations.idiomatic: Add the Duke of Tang's own troops, numbering tens of thousands—once the order is given, who would not follow?

sentences.zh: 鼓而入關，以震天下，王業成矣。

translations.literal: Beat drums and enter the passes to shake the realm, and the royal enterprise will be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Beat the drums, march through the passes, and shake the empire—and the royal enterprise will be won.

sentences.zh: 」王笑曰：「君言正與我意合。

translations.literal: " The prince smiled and said: "Your words match my intent exactly.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince smiled and said, "Your words match my intent exactly.

sentences.zh: 」乃陰部署賓客。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he secretly deployed his retainers.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he began secretly to deploy his retainers.

sentences.zh: 將發，恐唐公不從，文靜謀因裴寂開說，於是介寂以交王，遂得進議。

translations.literal: When they were about to act, fearing the Duke of Tang would not follow, Wenjing plotted to have Pei Ji open the way through persuasion; thus he had Ji introduced to the prince as intermediary and so gained entry to present his plan.
translations.idiomatic: As they prepared to move, Wenjing feared the Duke of Tang would not agree. He therefore planned to have Pei Ji persuade him first, and used Ji as intermediary to reach the Prince of Qin, thereby gaining access to present his proposal.

sentences.zh: 及突厥敗高君雅兵，唐公被劾，王遣文靜、寂共說曰：「公據嫌疑之地，勢不圖全。

translations.literal: When the Turks defeated Gao Junya's army and the Duke of Tang was impeached, the prince sent Wenjing and Ji together to persuade him, saying: "Your Lordship occupies a position under suspicion—in such circumstances one cannot plan for complete safety.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks defeated Gao Junya's army and the Duke of Tang came under impeachment, the Prince of Qin sent Wenjing and Ji together to urge him, saying, "Your Lordship stands in a position of suspicion; under such circumstances there is no safe course.

sentences.zh: 今部將敗，方以罪見收，事急矣，尚不為計乎？

translations.literal: Now your subordinates are defeated and you face arrest on criminal charges—the matter is urgent; will you still not make plans?
translations.idiomatic: Your subordinate has just been defeated, and you yourself are about to be seized on criminal charges. The crisis is upon us—will you still do nothing?

sentences.zh: 晉陽兵精馬強，宮庫饒豐，大事可舉也。

translations.literal: The troops of Jinyang are elite and the horses strong; the palace stores are abundantly full—the great enterprise can be raised.
translations.idiomatic: The troops at Jinyang are crack soldiers on strong horses, and the palace stores are overflowing. The great enterprise can be launched.

sentences.zh: 今關中空虛，代王弱，賢豪並興，未有適歸，願公引兵西，誅暴除亂。

translations.literal: Now the Guanzhong region is empty, the Prince of Dai is weak, worthy heroes rise together and none yet has found a proper allegiance—we ask Your Lordship to lead troops west to punish the violent and remove chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong is hollowed out, the Prince of Dai is weak, and worthy men are rising everywhere with nowhere rightful to turn. We ask Your Lordship to lead an army west to punish the violent and end the chaos.

sentences.zh: 乃受單使囚乎？

translations.literal: Will you instead accept being bound as a solitary envoy's prisoner?
translations.idiomatic: Or will you submit to arrest and imprisonment as a lone envoy?

sentences.zh: 」唐公私可，會得釋而止。

translations.literal: " The Duke of Tang privately consented, but when they obtained release the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The Duke of Tang privately agreed, but when they were released from the charges the plan was set aside.

sentences.zh: 王教文靜偽為詔「發太原、西河、雁門、馬邑男子年二十至五十悉為兵，期歲盡集涿郡以伐遼。

translations.literal: The prince instructed Wenjing to forge an edict: "Mobilize all men aged twenty to fifty from Taiyuan, Xihe, Yanmen, and Mayi as soldiers; within the year all are to assemble at Zhuo Commandery to campaign against Liao.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin had Wenjing forge an edict: "Mobilize all men between twenty and fifty from Taiyuan, Xihe, Yanmen, and Mayi. Within one year they are all to assemble at Zhuo Commandery for the campaign against Liao.

sentences.zh: 」繇是人心愁擾，益思亂。

translations.literal: " From this the people's hearts were troubled with worry and they thought all the more of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " From this the people grew anxious and restless, and thought all the more of revolt.

sentences.zh: 文靜謂寂曰：「公聞先發制人，後發制於人乎？

translations.literal: Wenjing said to Ji: "Have you heard that he who strikes first controls others, while he who strikes later is controlled by others?
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing said to Ji, "Have you heard the saying that he who strikes first controls others, while he who strikes later is controlled by others?

sentences.zh: 唐公名載圖讖，聞天下，尚可怗怗以待禍哉？

translations.literal: Duke Tang's name appears in prophecy charts and is known throughout the realm—can he still sit quietly and await disaster?
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Tang's name appears in prophetic texts and is known throughout the realm. Can he still sit quietly and wait for ruin?

sentences.zh: 」又脅寂曰：「公為監，以宮人侍客，公死何憾，奈何累唐公？

translations.literal: " He further coerced Ji, saying: "You as overseer provided palace women to entertain guests—what regret would your death bring? But why drag down Duke Tang?
translations.idiomatic: " He then pressed Ji, saying, "As overseer you provided palace women to entertain guests. Your own death would be no great loss—but why drag the Duke of Tang down with you?

sentences.zh: 」寂懼，乃勸起兵。

translations.literal: " Ji feared, and so urged raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji was frightened and thereupon urged that they raise troops.

sentences.zh: 秦王即委文靜、長孫順德等募士，聲討劉武周。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin then entrusted Wenjing, Zhangsun Shunde, and others to recruit warriors, publicly announcing a campaign against Liu Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin then put Wenjing, Zhangsun Shunde, and others in charge of recruiting troops, publicly proclaiming a campaign against Liu Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 文靜與寂作符敕，發宮監庫物佐軍興。

translations.literal: Wenjing and Ji made tally-edicts and issued goods from the palace overseer's stores to support the army's mobilization.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing and Ji drew up tally-orders and released goods from the palace overseer's stores to supply the rising army.

sentences.zh: 會王威、高君雅猜貳，文靜與劉政會為急變書，詣留守告二人反，候唐公與威、君雅視事，文靜進曰：「有密牒言反者。

translations.literal: When Wang Wei and Gao Junya became suspicious and wavering, Wenjing and Liu Zhenghui wrote an urgent report accusing the two of rebellion; proceeding to the garrison headquarters to inform on them, they waited until the Duke of Tang was attending to business with Wei and Junya, and Wenjing stepped forward saying: "There is a secret report concerning rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Wei and Gao Junya grew suspicious and unreliable, Wenjing and Liu Zhenghui drafted an urgent report accusing the two of rebellion. They went to the garrison headquarters to denounce them, and when the Duke of Tang was conducting business with Wei and Junya, Wenjing stepped forward and said, "There is a secret report of treason.

sentences.zh: 」公目威等省牒，政會不肯，曰：「所告乃副留守，唯唐公得觀。

translations.literal: " The duke signaled Wei and the others to read the report; Zhenghui refused, saying: "The accused are the deputy garrison commanders—only Duke Tang may view it.
translations.idiomatic: " The duke signaled for Wei and the others to read the report, but Zhenghui refused, saying, "The accused are the deputy garrison commanders. Only the Duke of Tang may view it.

sentences.zh: 」公驚曰：「詎有是乎？

translations.literal: " The duke said in alarm: "Could there really be such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: " The duke said in alarm, "Can this really be?

sentences.zh: 」讀已，語威曰：「人告公等，信乎？

translations.literal: " After reading it, he said to Wei: "Men report against you—do you believe it?
translations.idiomatic: " After reading it, he said to Wei, "Men have accused you—do you believe it?

sentences.zh: 」君雅詬曰：「反人欲殺我耳。

translations.literal: " Junya cursed and said: "The rebels simply want to kill me.
translations.idiomatic: " Junya cursed and said, "The rebels simply want to kill me.

sentences.zh: 文靜叱左右執之，由是舉兵。

translations.literal: Wenjing shouted at the attendants to seize them, and thereby troops were raised.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing ordered the attendants to seize them, and with that the army was raised.

sentences.zh: 唐公乃開大將軍府，以文靜為司馬。

translations.literal: The Duke of Tang then opened the Grand General's Office and appointed Wenjing as Chief of Staff.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Tang then established the Grand General's Office and appointed Wenjing chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 文靜勸改旗幟，彰特興，又請與突厥連和，唐公從之。

translations.literal: Wenjing urged changing banners and standards to proclaim the Tang's distinctive rise, and also requested alliance with the Turks; the Duke of Tang followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing urged that they change their banners and standards to proclaim the distinctive rise of the Tang, and also asked to ally with the Turks. The Duke of Tang agreed.

sentences.zh: 遣文靜使始畢可汗，始畢曰：「唐公兵何事而起？

translations.literal: He dispatched Wenjing as envoy to Shibi Khagan, who said: "For what affair does Duke Tang's army rise?
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wenjing as envoy to Shibi Khagan. Shibi asked, "For what reason has the Duke of Tang raised an army?

sentences.zh: 」文靜曰：「先帝廢冢嗣以授後主，故大亂。

translations.literal: " Wenjing said: "The late emperor set aside the heir and gave the throne to a later ruler; hence great chaos.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenjing said, "The late emperor set aside the crown prince and gave the throne to a lesser ruler, and so the realm fell into great chaos.

sentences.zh: 唐公，國近戚，懼毀王室，起兵黜不當立者。

translations.literal: Duke Tang, a close kin of the dynasty, feared the destruction of the royal house and raised troops to depose one unfit to be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Tang is a close kinsman of the imperial house. Fearing the ruin of the royal line, he has raised troops to remove one who ought not to reign.

sentences.zh: 願與突厥共定京師，金幣、子女盡以歸可汗。

translations.literal: We wish jointly with the Turks to settle the capital; gold, silk, and women will all be given to the khagan.
translations.idiomatic: We wish to join with the Turks in pacifying the capital. All gold, silk, and captives shall go to the khagan.

sentences.zh: 」始畢大喜，即遣二千騎隨文靜至，又獻馬千匹。

translations.literal: " Shibi was greatly pleased and immediately sent two thousand horsemen to follow Wenjing's arrival, and also presented a thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: " Shibi was greatly pleased and immediately sent two thousand horsemen to accompany Wenjing, and also presented a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 公喜曰：「非君何以致之？

translations.literal: The duke said with pleasure: "Without you, how could this have been obtained?
translations.idiomatic: The duke said with delight, "Without you, how could this have been achieved?

sentences.zh: 」尋拒屈突通於潼關，與其將桑顯和苦鬥，死者數千。

translations.literal: " Soon they repelled Qu Tuotong at Tong Pass and fought bitterly with his general Sang Xianhe—several thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward they held Qu Tuotong at Tong Pass and fought bitterly with his general Sang Xianhe; several thousand men were killed.

sentences.zh: 文靜度顯和軍怠，以奇兵從後掩之，顯和敗績。

translations.literal: Wenjing judged Xianhe's army slack and sent surprise troops to strike from behind; Xianhe suffered a crushing defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing judged that Xianhe's army had grown lax and sent a surprise force to strike from the rear. Xianhe was routed.

sentences.zh: 通兵尚數萬，欲引而東，文靜命將追執之，徇新安以西，皆下。

translations.literal: Tong's troops still numbered tens of thousands and he wished to withdraw eastward; Wenjing ordered generals to pursue and capture him, marched through displaying the victory west of Xin'an, and all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tuotong still had tens of thousands of troops and intended to withdraw eastward. Wenjing ordered his generals to pursue and capture him, then marched west from Xin'an subduing the region; all submitted.

sentences.zh: 轉大丞相府司馬，進光祿大夫、魯國公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief of Staff of the Grand Chancellor's Office, promoted to Minister of the Imperial Clan and Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief of staff of the Grand Chancellor's Office and promoted to Minister of the Imperial Clan and Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 唐公踐天子位，擢納言。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Tang ascended the imperial throne, Wenjing was elevated to Chief Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Tang ascended the throne as emperor, Wenjing was promoted to chief censor.

sentences.zh: 時多引貴臣共榻，文靜諫曰：「今率土莫不臣，而延見群下，言尚稱名。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor often summoned eminent ministers to share his couch; Wenjing remonstrated, saying: "Now all within the realm are subjects, yet in extending audience to subordinates speech still uses personal names.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor often summoned eminent ministers to sit with him on the same couch. Wenjing remonstrated, saying, "All within the realm are now subjects, yet when Your Majesty receives officials below, they still address you by personal name.

sentences.zh: 帝坐嚴尊，屈與臣子均席，此王導所謂太陽俯同萬物者也。

translations.literal: The emperor's seat is solemnly exalted, yet he stoops to share a mat equally with ministers—this is what Wang Dao called the sun bowing level with all things.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial seat is solemn and exalted, yet Your Majesty stoops to share a mat equally with your ministers. This is what Wang Dao meant when he said the sun bends down level with all things beneath it.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「我雖應天受命，宿昔之好何可忘？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Though I have received Heaven's mandate, how can I forget old friendship?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Though I have received Heaven's mandate, how can I forget old friendship?

sentences.zh: 公其無嫌。

translations.literal: Sir, do not be reserved.
translations.idiomatic: Do not be so reserved.

sentences.zh: 」薛舉寇涇州，以元帥府長史與司馬殷開山出戰，大敗，奔還京師，坐除名。

translations.literal: " When Xue Ju invaded Jing Prefecture, Wenjing as chief of staff of the commander's office went out to battle with the Chief of Staff Yin Kaishan and suffered great defeat; he fled back to the capital and was stripped of rank and ennoblement.
translations.idiomatic: " When Xue Ju invaded Jing Prefecture, Wenjing went out to battle as chief of staff of the commander's office together with the chief of staff Yin Kaishan and suffered a crushing defeat. He fled back to the capital and was stripped of rank and title.

sentences.zh: 與討仁杲，平之，復爵邑，授民部尚書、陜東道行臺左僕射。

translations.literal: He accompanied the campaign against Ren Jie and pacified him, had his title and fief restored, and was appointed Minister of Revenue and Left Vice Director of the Shaanxi-East Circuit Mobile Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Ren Jie and pacified him. His title and fief were restored, and he was appointed Minister of Revenue and Left Vice Director of the Shaanxi-East Circuit Mobile Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從秦王鎮長春宮。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Qin in garrisoning Changchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Qin to garrison Changchun Palace.

sentences.zh: 文靜自以材能過裴寂遠甚，又屢有軍功，而寂獨用故舊恩居其上，意不平。

translations.literal: Wenjing considered his talent far superior to Pei Ji's and had repeatedly won military merit, yet Ji alone relied on old friendship and sat above him—his heart was not at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing considered his ability far superior to Pei Ji's and had repeatedly won military distinction, yet Ji alone, by virtue of old friendship, stood above him. Wenjing's heart was not at peace.

sentences.zh: 每論政多戾駁，遂有隙。

translations.literal: Whenever they discussed policy he often spoke contrarily, and thereby a rift developed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they discussed policy he often contradicted Ji, and a rift opened between them.

sentences.zh: 嘗與弟散騎常侍文起飲酣，有怨言，拔刀擊柱曰：「當斬寂！

translations.literal: Once, drinking heavily with his younger brother Wenqi, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, he voiced complaints, drew his sword and struck a pillar, saying: "I ought to behead Ji!
translations.idiomatic: Once, drinking heavily with his younger brother Wenqi, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, he gave voice to his grievances, drew his sword, and struck a pillar, crying, "I ought to cut Ji down!

sentences.zh: 」會家數有怪，文起憂，召巫夜被發銜刀為禳厭。

translations.literal: " Just then there were several uncanny occurrences in the family; Wenqi worried and summoned a shaman who at night let down his hair and held a knife in his mouth to perform exorcism.
translations.idiomatic: " About that time several strange occurrences troubled the household. Wenqi grew anxious and summoned a shaman, who at night let down his hair and held a knife in his mouth to perform an exorcism.

sentences.zh: 文靜妾失愛，告其兄上變，遂下吏。

translations.literal: Wenjing's concubine, having fallen from favor, reported the affair to her elder brother as an accusation of treason, and he was turned over to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing's concubine, having lost his favor, reported the matter through her elder brother as an accusation of treason, and Wenjing was handed over to the officials.

sentences.zh: 帝遣裴寂、蕭瑀訊狀，對曰：「昔在大將軍府，司馬與長史略等。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Pei Ji and Xiao Yu to examine the case; Wenjing replied: "Formerly in the Grand General's Office, the Chief of Staff and the Chief Administrator were roughly equal in rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Pei Ji and Xiao Yu to investigate. Wenjing replied, "In the early days at the Grand General's Office, the chief of staff and the chief administrator were roughly equal in rank.

sentences.zh: 今寂已僕射，居甲第，寵賚不貲。

translations.literal: Now Ji is already Vice Chancellor, dwelling in a mansion of the first rank, his gifts and rewards beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Now Ji is vice chancellor, living in a mansion of the first rank, his gifts and rewards beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 臣官賞等眾人，家無贏，誠不能無少望。

translations.literal: My office and rewards are the same as the common run; my household has no surplus—truly I cannot be without a little resentment.
translations.idiomatic: My office and rewards are no different from those of ordinary men, and my household has no surplus. Truly I cannot be entirely free of resentment.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「文靜此言，反明甚。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "In these words Wenjing's intent to rebel is quite clear.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "In these words Wenjing's intent to rebel is all too clear.

sentences.zh: 」李綱、蕭瑀明其不反；

translations.literal: " Li Gang and Xiao Yu made clear he was not rebelling;
translations.idiomatic: " Li Gang and Xiao Yu made clear that he was not rebelling;

sentences.zh: 秦王亦以文靜首決非常計，事成乃告寂，今任遇弗等，故怨望，非敢反，宜賜全宥。

translations.literal: the Prince of Qin also held that Wenjing first resolved the extraordinary plan; only after success did he inform Ji—now their appointments and treatment were unequal, hence his resentment; he did not dare rebel, and they should grant full pardon.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Qin also argued that Wenjing had been the first to resolve the extraordinary plan and had informed Ji only after success. Now that their appointments and favor were unequal, his resentment was understandable; he did not truly mean to rebel, and they ought to grant him full pardon.

sentences.zh: 帝素疏忌之，寂又言：「文靜多權詭，而性猜險，忿不顧難，醜言怪節已暴驗，今天下未靖，恐為後憂。

translations.literal: The emperor had long kept his distance and harbored suspicion; Ji further said: "Wenjing is full of stratagems and cunning, and by nature suspicious and perilous—when angry he heedless of difficulty; his ugly words and strange conduct have already been plainly verified; the realm is not yet settled—we fear he may become a future worry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long kept his distance and harbored suspicion toward him. Ji added, "Wenjing is full of stratagems and cunning, and by nature suspicious and dangerous. When angered he reckons nothing of difficulty. His ugly words and strange conduct have already been plainly seen. The realm is not yet settled, and I fear he may become a source of trouble later.

sentences.zh: 」帝遂殺之，年五十二。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon executed him, at age fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon had him executed. He was fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 文起亦死，籍其家。

translations.literal: Wenqi also died, and their household property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqi was executed as well, and their household property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 文靜臨刑，撫膺曰：「高鳥盡，良弓藏，果不妄。

translations.literal: At execution Wenjing clutched his chest and said: "When the high birds are gone, the good bows are stored away—indeed not wrongly spoken.
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution, Wenjing clutched his chest and said, "When the high birds are gone, the good bows are stored away—the saying is no empty phrase.

sentences.zh: 」貞觀三年，追復官爵，以子樹義襲魯國公，詔尚主。

translations.literal: " In the third year of Zhenguan his office and title were posthumously restored; his son Shuyi inherited the dukedom of Lu, with an edict granting marriage to an imperial princess.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third year of Zhenguan his office and title were posthumously restored. His son Shuyi inherited the dukedom of Lu, and an edict granted him marriage to an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 然怨父不得死，謀反，誅。

translations.literal: Yet resenting that his father had not been permitted a natural death, he plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet, resenting his father's unjust execution, he plotted rebellion and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 裴寂，字玄真，蒲州桑泉人。

translations.literal: Pei Ji, courtesy name Xuanzhen, was a native of Sangquan in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji, courtesy name Xuanzhen, was a native of Sangquan in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，兄鞠之。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, his elder brother raised him.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in childhood, he was raised by his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 年十四，補郡主簿。

translations.literal: At fourteen he was appointed prefectural chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he was appointed chief clerk of his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及長，偉容貌，涉知書傳。

translations.literal: When grown, he had a grand appearance and breadth of learning in classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he had a striking appearance and a working knowledge of the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，調左親衛。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was assigned to the Left Personal Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty he was assigned to the Left Personal Guard.

sentences.zh: 家貧，徙步走京師，過華山祠，祈神自卜，夜夢老人謂曰：「君年逾四十當貴。」

translations.literal: His family was poor; he walked on foot to the capital. Passing the temple on Mount Hua he prayed to the god to divine his fortune; at night he dreamed an old man told him: "Past forty years you will attain eminence."
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, and he walked on foot to the capital. Passing the shrine on Mount Hua, he prayed to the god to divine his fortune. That night he dreamed that an old man told him, "After you pass forty you will rise to eminence."

sentences.zh: 大業中，為齊州司戶參軍，歷侍御史，晉陽宮副監。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he served as Registrar of Qi Prefecture, then Gentleman Auditor, and Deputy Overseer of the Jinyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era he served as registrar of Qi Prefecture, then as gentleman auditor and deputy overseer of the Jinyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 唐公雅與厚，及留守太原，契分愈密，至蒲酒通晝夜。

translations.literal: The Duke of Tang had long been close with him; when he remained as garrison commander at Taiyuan their bond grew ever closer, drinking together day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Tang had long been on close terms with him. When he took up garrison duty at Taiyuan their bond grew ever closer, and they drank together day and night.

sentences.zh: 秦王與劉文靜方建大計，未敢白公，以寂最厚善，乃同私錢數百萬餉龍山令高斌廉，俾與寂博，陽不勝，寂得進多，大喜，日滋昵。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin and Liu Wenjing were just forging the great plan and did not dare inform the duke; because Ji was closest in friendship, they used several million in private funds to supply Longshan Magistrate Gao Binian, enabling him to gamble with Ji—feigning loss, Ji won heavily, was greatly pleased, and day by day grew more intimate.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin and Liu Wenjing were just forming their great plan and did not yet dare tell the duke. Because Ji was their closest friend, they pooled several million in private funds and gave them to Longshan Magistrate Gao Binian so that he could gamble with Ji. Binian feigned defeat, Ji won heavily, was greatly pleased, and day by day grew more intimate with them.

sentences.zh: 太宗以情告之，許諾。

translations.literal: Taizong told him the full situation in confidence, and he agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin confided the whole plan to him, and Ji agreed.

sentences.zh: 寂嘗以宮人侍唐公，恐事發誅，閑飲酣，乃白秦王將舉兵狀，因言：「今盜遍天下，城闔外即戰場，雖徇小節，猶不脫死。

translations.literal: Ji had once provided palace women to serve the Duke of Tang; fearing exposure and execution, during a leisurely bout of heavy drinking he told the Prince of Qin of the plan to raise troops, saying: "Now bandits fill the realm—beyond the city gates lies the battlefield; even if one observes small proprieties, one still cannot escape death.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had once provided palace women to attend the Duke of Tang. Fearing exposure and execution, during a bout of heavy drinking he told the Prince of Qin of the plan to raise troops, saying, "Bandits now fill the realm. Beyond the city gates lies nothing but battlefield. Even if one clings to small proprieties, one still cannot escape death.

sentences.zh: 若舉義師，不特免禍，且就大功。

translations.literal: If we raise the army of righteousness, not only will we escape disaster, but we will achieve great merit as well.
translations.idiomatic: If we raise the army of righteousness, we will not only escape disaster but win great merit as well.

sentences.zh: 」唐公然所計。

translations.literal: " The Duke of Tang approved his plan.
translations.idiomatic: " The Duke of Tang approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 兵起，寂進宮女五百，米九百萬斛，雜彩五萬段，鎧四十萬首。

translations.literal: When troops were raised, Ji presented five hundred palace women, nine million hu of grain, fifty thousand bolts of assorted silks, and four hundred thousand sets of armor.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was raised, Ji contributed five hundred palace women, nine million hu of grain, fifty thousand bolts of assorted silks, and four hundred thousand suits of armor.

sentences.zh: 大將軍府建，為長史。

translations.literal: When the Grand General's Office was established, he was made Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand General's Office was established, he was appointed chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 下臨汾，封聞喜縣公。

translations.literal: When they descended on Linfen he was enfeoffed as Duke of Wenxi County.
translations.idiomatic: After they took Linfen he was enfeoffed as Duke of Wenxi County.

sentences.zh: 至河東，屈突通未下，而三輔豪傑多歸者。

translations.literal: Reaching Hedong, Qu Tuotong had not yet been taken, yet many heroes of the Three Metropolises region had already submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Hedong, Qu Tuotong had not yet been subdued, but many leading men of the Three Metropolises region had already come over to their side.

sentences.zh: 唐公欲先取京師，恐通掎其後，猶豫未決，寂說曰：「今通據蒲關，未下而西，我腹背支敵，敗之符也。

translations.literal: The Duke of Tang wished to take the capital first but feared that Tong would strike from behind; hesitating, he could not decide. Ji persuaded him, saying: "Now Tong holds Puguan Pass. If we go west before he is subdued, we shall be attacked front and rear—a sign of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Tang wanted to seize the capital first but feared Qu Tuotong would strike from the rear, and he hesitated, unable to decide. Pei Ji urged him, saying, "Qu Tuotong now holds Puguan Pass. If we march west before he falls, we will be caught between two enemies—that is a recipe for defeat.

sentences.zh: 不若破通而後趨京師。

translations.literal: Better to break Tong first and then hurry to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Better to defeat Qu Tuotong first, then rush on to the capital.

sentences.zh: 」秦王曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " The Prince of Qin said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince of Qin said, "No.

sentences.zh: 兵尚權，權利於速。

translations.literal: War values flexibility, and flexibility lies in speed.
translations.idiomatic: In war one must be flexible, and flexibility means acting swiftly.

sentences.zh: 今乘機度河以奪其心。

translations.literal: Now seize the moment, cross the river, and seize their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Now we should seize the moment, cross the river, and win them over.

sentences.zh: 且關中群盜處處屯結，疑力相杖，易以招懷，撫而有之，眾附兵強，何向不克。

translations.literal: Moreover, bandits throughout Guanzhong are gathered everywhere in fortified camps, lending one another strength in mutual suspicion; they are easy to win over and pacify. Once embraced and possessed, the people will attach themselves and the army will grow strong—what direction could we not conquer?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, bandits throughout Guanzhong are encamped everywhere, backing one another's strength. They can easily be won over and brought under control. Once we pacify and hold them, the people will rally to us and our forces will grow—what could we not take?

sentences.zh: 通自守賊耳，庸能患我？

translations.literal: Tong is merely a defensive bandit—how could he trouble us?
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tuotong is only a defensive rebel—how could he truly threaten us?

sentences.zh: 一失其機，勝負未可計也。

translations.literal: Once the opportunity is lost, victory and defeat cannot be calculated.
translations.idiomatic: Miss this chance, and victory or defeat become impossible to foretell.

sentences.zh: 」唐公兩從之，留兵圍蒲，而遣秦王入關。

translations.literal: " The Duke of Tang adopted both views in part, left troops to besiege Pu, and sent the Prince of Qin to enter the pass.
translations.idiomatic: " The Duke of Tang took something from both counsels: he left troops to besiege Pu and sent the Prince of Qin through the pass into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 長安平，賜寂田千頃、甲第一區，物四萬段，遷大丞相府長史，進魏國公，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified, Ji was granted a thousand qing of fields, one first-ranked mansion, forty thousand bolts of goods, promoted to Chief Administrator of the Grand Chancellor's Office, advanced to Duke of Wei with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an was pacified, Pei Ji was granted a thousand qing of land, a first-ranked mansion, and forty thousand bolts of goods. He was promoted to chief administrator of the Grand Chancellor's Office and advanced to Duke of Wei with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，劉武周寇太原，守將數困，寂請行，授晉州道行軍總管討賊，以便宜決事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude, Liu Wuzhou raided Taiyuan and the garrison commanders were repeatedly hard pressed. Ji requested to take the field and was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Jinzhou Circuit Army to suppress the bandits, with authority to decide matters as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wude, Liu Wuzhou invaded Taiyuan and the defending generals were repeatedly driven into distress. Pei Ji asked to take command and was appointed commander-in-chief of the Jinzhou circuit army to suppress the rebels, with discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 賊將宋金剛據介州，寂屯度索原，賊埭水上流，寂徙屯，為賊所搏，兵大潰，死亡略盡。

translations.literal: The bandit general Song Jingang held Jie Prefecture. Ji encamped at Dusuo Plain; the bandits dammed the upper reaches of the water, and when Ji moved camp he was struck by them. The army collapsed in great rout, and the dead were nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Song Jingang held Jie Prefecture. Pei Ji encamped at Dusuo Plain; the rebels dammed the upstream waters, and when he shifted camp they struck. His army broke in a catastrophic rout, and nearly all his men were killed.

sentences.zh: 寂晝夜馳抵平陽，鎮戍皆沒。

translations.literal: Ji raced day and night to reach Pingyang; the garrison posts were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji rode day and night to reach Pingyang, but every fortified post along the way had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 上書謝罪，高祖薄其過，下詔慰諭，俾留撫河東。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial asking forgiveness. Gaozu treated his fault lightly, issued an edict to comfort and instruct him, and ordered him to remain and pacify Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial asking pardon. Emperor Gaozu treated his fault leniently, issued an edict of consolation, and ordered him to remain in Hedong to restore order.

sentences.zh: 寂無它才，惟飛檄郡縣，促入屯壘相保贅，焚積聚，人益惴駭思亂。

translations.literal: Ji had no other talent; he only sent urgent dispatches to the commanderies and counties, pressing people into fortified camps for mutual protection, burning stored supplies, and the people grew ever more fearful and inclined to revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji had no other gift for the task. He merely sent urgent dispatches to the commanderies and counties, forcing people into fortified camps for mutual protection and burning stored grain. The populace grew ever more terrified and restless.

sentences.zh: 夏人呂崇茂殺其令，反，為賊守，寂攻之，復為所敗。

translations.literal: A man of Xia, Lü Chongmao, killed his magistrate and rebelled, holding the place for the bandits. Ji attacked him and was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: A local man named Lü Chongmao killed his magistrate and rebelled, holding the town for the enemy. Pei Ji attacked him and was defeated again.

sentences.zh: 召還，帝責讓良久，以屬吏，俄釋之，遇待如初。

translations.literal: He was recalled; the emperor reproached him at length, handed him over to the officials, but soon released him and treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court. Emperor Gaozu rebuked him at length and handed him over to the judicial officials, but soon released him and treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 帝每巡幸，必委以居守。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went on tour, he always entrusted Ji to remain and guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Gaozu traveled, he always left Pei Ji in charge of the capital.

sentences.zh: 麟州刺史韋雲起告寂反，按訊無狀，帝謂曰：「朕有天下，公推轂成之也，容有貳哉？

translations.literal: Lin Prefecture Inspector Wei Yunqi reported that Ji was plotting rebellion. Investigation found no substance. The emperor said to him: "I have gained the realm—your pushing the chariot wheel made it so. How could you harbor disloyalty?
translations.idiomatic: Lin Prefecture inspector Wei Yunqi reported that Pei Ji was plotting rebellion. Investigation found nothing to support the charge. Emperor Gaozu told him, "I won the realm—you helped push the chariot wheel that brought me here. How could you turn against me?

sentences.zh: 所以訊吏，欲天下人信公不反耳。

translations.literal: The reason I questioned the officials was to make everyone under Heaven believe that you would not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I had the officials examine the case was so that all under Heaven would believe you had not rebelled.

sentences.zh: 」詔三貴妃賫玉食寶器宴其家，經宿去。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered three imperial consorts to carry jade foods and precious vessels to feast at his home; they stayed overnight and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered three imperial consorts to bring jade dishes and precious vessels to feast at Pei Ji's home. They stayed the night and then departed.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗從容誇語曰：「前王多興細微，間關行陣而後成功。

translations.literal: The emperor once spoke at leisure in boastful tones, saying: "Former kings mostly rose from humble origins, passing through hardship and battle before succeeding.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu once spoke at leisure in a boastful vein, saying, "Former kings mostly rose from humble beginnings, struggling through hardship and battle before they succeeded.

sentences.zh: 我家隴西舊族，世姻婭帝室，一呼倡義，不三月有天下，公復華胄，職宦光顯，非劉季亭長、蕭曹刀筆吏比也。

translations.literal: My house is an old clan of Longxi, for generations allied by marriage to the imperial house. At one call we raised righteousness, and in less than three months we had the realm. You too are of illustrious ancestry, with offices shining bright—not to be compared with Liu Ji the pavilion chief or Xiao and Cao the clerks with their writing knives.
translations.idiomatic: My house is an old Longxi clan, bound by marriage to the imperial line for generations. At a single call to arms we won the realm in less than three months. You too are of noble lineage, with a distinguished official career—not to be compared with Liu Bang the pavilion chief or Xiao He and Cao Shen, mere clerks with their writing knives.

sentences.zh: 我與公無愧焉。

translations.literal: You and I have nothing to be ashamed of.
translations.idiomatic: You and I have nothing to be ashamed of between us.

sentences.zh: 」四年，改鑄錢，賜一爐得自鑄。

translations.literal: " In the fourth year, coinage was reformed, and he was granted one furnace to cast coin for himself.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourth year, when coinage was reformed, he was granted one minting furnace for his private use.

sentences.zh: 又聘其女為趙王元景妃。

translations.literal: His daughter was also betrothed as consort to Prince Zhao, Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was also betrothed to Prince Zhao, Li Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 遷左僕射。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝置酒含章殿，歡甚，寂頓首曰：「始陛下發太原，約天下已定，許上印綬。

translations.literal: The emperor set wine in Hanzhang Hall and was exceedingly merry. Ji bowed his head and said: "At the beginning, when Your Majesty raised troops at Taiyuan, you promised that once the realm was settled you would grant me my seal and sash.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu held a banquet in Hanzhang Hall and was in high spirits. Pei Ji bowed low and said, "When Your Majesty first raised troops at Taiyuan, you promised that once the realm was settled you would let me surrender my seal and sash.

sentences.zh: 今四海妥安，願賜骸骨歸田裏。

translations.literal: Now the four seas are secure; I beg to be granted my bones and return to my fields.
translations.idiomatic: Now the four seas are at peace. I beg leave to retire and return to my home.

sentences.zh: 」帝泣下曰：「未也，要當相與老爾。

translations.literal: " The emperor wept and said: "Not yet—we must grow old together.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozu wept and said, "Not yet. We must grow old together.

sentences.zh: 公為宗臣，我為太上皇，逍遙晚歲，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: You shall be a minister of the imperial clan, and I shall be Retired Emperor; roaming freely in our later years—is that not good!
translations.idiomatic: You will remain a pillar of the dynasty, and I shall become Retired Emperor. We shall spend our later years in ease—is that not fine?

sentences.zh: 」九年，冊拜司空，遣尚書員外郎日一人直第。

translations.literal: " In the ninth year he was enfeoffed as Minister of Works, and one Secretariat aide was sent daily to attend at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: " In the ninth year he was enfeoffed as Minister of Works, and one Secretariat aide was dispatched each day to attend at his residence.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，太宗親郊，命寂與長孫無忌升金輅，寂辭，帝曰：「公有佐命勛，無忌宣力王室，非二人誰可參乘者？

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Taizong personally performed the suburban sacrifice and ordered Ji and Zhangsun Wuji to ascend the gilded chariot. Ji declined. The emperor said: "You have merit in aiding the mandate; Wuji has exerted his strength for the royal house—if not you two, who may ride as companions?
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era, Emperor Taizong personally performed the suburban sacrifice and ordered Pei Ji and Zhangsun Wuji to ascend the gilded imperial chariot. Pei Ji declined. The emperor said, "You aided the founding mandate, and Wuji has served the royal house with all his strength. If not the two of you, who else could ride as my companions?

sentences.zh: 」遂同載歸。

translations.literal: " They then rode back together.
translations.idiomatic: " They then rode back together.

sentences.zh: 浮屠法雅坐妖言，辭連寂，坐免官，削封邑半，歸故郡。

translations.literal: The Buddhist monk Fayi was convicted of seditious speech; his testimony implicated Ji. Ji was removed from office, half his fief was cut, and he was sent back to his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddhist monk Fayi was convicted of spreading seditious talk, and his testimony implicated Pei Ji. Pei Ji was dismissed from office, half his fief was stripped, and he was sent back to his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 寂請留京師，帝讓曰：「公勛不稱位，徙以恩澤居第一。

translations.literal: Ji requested to remain in the capital. The emperor reproached him, saying: "Your merit does not match your rank; you sit in first place only through favor.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji asked to remain in the capital. The emperor rebuked him, saying, "Your merit does not match your rank. You hold first place only through imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 武德之政，間或弛紊，職公為之。

translations.literal: The slackness and disorder of Wude-era governance were in part your doing.
translations.idiomatic: The laxity and disorder of Wude-era governance were in part your doing.

sentences.zh: 今歸掃墳墓，尚何辭？

translations.literal: Now return and sweep your ancestors' tombs—what further plea can you make?
translations.idiomatic: Go home and tend your ancestors' graves—what further argument can you offer?

sentences.zh: 」寂遂歸。

translations.literal: " Ji then returned.
translations.idiomatic: " Pei Ji then departed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，汾陰狂男子謂寂奴曰：「公有天分。

translations.literal: Before long, a madman at Fenyin said to Ji's household slave: "Your master has the mandate of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, a madman at Fenyin said to one of Pei Ji's household slaves, "Your master has Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 」監奴白寂，寂惶懼不敢聞，遣監奴殺所言者。

translations.literal: " The supervising slave reported to Ji. Ji was fearful and dared not inform the throne; he sent the slave to kill the speaker.
translations.idiomatic: " The supervising slave reported this to Pei Ji. Pei Ji was terrified and dared not report it. He sent the slave to kill the man who had spoken.

sentences.zh: 奴盜寂封邑錢百萬，寂捕急，遂上變。

translations.literal: The slave stole a million in cash from Ji's fief income. When Ji pressed the arrest, the slave submitted a denunciation.
translations.idiomatic: The slave stole a million in cash from Pei Ji's fief income. When Pei Ji pressed hard for his arrest, the slave submitted a denunciation to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「寂有死罪四：為三公，與妖人遊，一也；

translations.literal: The emperor said in anger: "Ji has four capital offenses: as one of the Three Dukes he consorted with sorcerers—that is the first;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said angrily, "Pei Ji deserves death on four counts: as one of the Three Dukes he consorted with sorcerers—that is the first;

sentences.zh: 既免官，乃恚稱國家之興皆其所謀，二也；

translations.literal: having been dismissed from office, he still resentfully claimed that the rise of the state was all due to his plotting—that is the second;
translations.idiomatic: after dismissal he still resentfully claimed the founding of the state was all his doing—that is the second;

sentences.zh: 匿妖人言不奏，三也；

translations.literal: he concealed the sorcerer's words and did not report them—that is the third;
translations.idiomatic: he concealed the madman's words and failed to report them—that is the third;

sentences.zh: 專殺以滅口，四也。

translations.literal: he killed on his own authority to silence witnesses—that is the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: he executed a man on his own authority to silence him—that is the fourth.

sentences.zh: 我戮之非無辭。

translations.literal: If I put him to death, it is not without grounds.
translations.idiomatic: If I execute him, I shall not be without cause.

sentences.zh: 」議者多請貸，乃放靜州。

translations.literal: " Many at court pleaded for leniency, and he was exiled to Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Many at court pleaded for mercy, and he was exiled to Jing Prefecture instead.

sentences.zh: 會山羌反，或言劫寂為主。

translations.literal: When the mountain Qiang rebelled, some said they would seize Ji and make him their leader.
translations.idiomatic: When the mountain Qiang rebelled, some said the rebels would seize Pei Ji and make him their leader.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「國家於寂有恩，必不爾。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The state has shown Ji kindness—he will surely not do so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The state has treated Pei Ji with kindness. He would surely never do such a thing.

sentences.zh: 」既而寂率家僮破賊。

translations.literal: " Before long Ji led his household retainers and broke the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long Pei Ji led his household retainers and defeated the rebels.

sentences.zh: 帝念寂功，詔入朝，會卒，年六十。

translations.literal: The emperor, remembering Ji's merit, issued an edict summoning him to court; he died on the way, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, remembering Pei Ji's service, issued an edict summoning him to court, but Pei Ji died on the journey at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈相州刺史、工部尚書、河東郡公。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Governor of Xiang Prefecture, Minister of Works, and Duke of Hedong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles of governor of Xiang Prefecture, Minister of Works, and Duke of Hedong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 子律師嗣，尚臨海長公主，終汴州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Lüshi inherited the title, married Princess Linhai, and ended as Governor of Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lüshi inherited the title, married Princess Linhai, and ended his career as governor of Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 律師子承先，武後時為殿中監，酷吏殺之。

translations.literal: Lüshi's son Chengxian, during Empress Wu's reign served as Director of the Palace Directorate and was killed by the cruel officials.
translations.idiomatic: Lüshi's son Chengxian served as director of the Palace Directorate under Empress Wu and was killed by the cruel officials.

sentences.zh: 始，高祖論太原首功，詔尚書令秦王、尚書左僕射裴寂、納言劉文靜恕二死；

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Gaozu assessed the first merit of Taiyuan, an edict granted the Prince of Qin as Director of the Secretariat, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Pei Ji, and Chief Counselor Liu Wenjing pardon for two capital offenses;
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, when Emperor Gaozu assessed the founding merit of Taiyuan, an edict granted the Prince of Qin as director of the Secretariat, Left Vice Director Pei Ji, and Chief Counselor Liu Wenjing pardon for two capital offenses;

sentences.zh: 左驍衛大將軍長孫順德、右驍衛大將軍劉弘基、右屯衛大將軍竇琮、左翊衛大將軍柴紹、內史侍郎唐儉、吏部侍郎殷開山、鴻臚卿劉世龍、衛尉少卿劉政會、都水監趙文恪、庫部郎中武士〓驃騎將軍張平高、李思行、李高遷、左屯衛府長史許世緒等十四人恕一死。

translations.literal: Left Brave Guard General Zhangsun Shunde, Right Brave Guard General Liu Hongji, Right Garrison Guard General Dou Cong, Left Flank Guard General Chai Shao, Secretariat Vice Minister Tang Jian, Ministry of Personnel Vice Minister Yin Kaishan, Grand Herald Liu Shilong, Court of Imperial Sacrifices Vice Minister Liu Zhenghui, Director of Waterways Zhao Wenke, Storehouse Bureau Director Wu Shihuo, Cavalry General Zhang Pinggao, Li Sixing, Li Gaoqian, Left Garrison Guard Office Chief Administrator Xu Shixu, and fourteen others pardon for one capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: Left Brave Guard general Zhangsun Shunde, Right Brave Guard general Liu Hongji, Right Garrison Guard general Dou Cong, Left Flank Guard general Chai Shao, Secretariat vice minister Tang Jian, Ministry of Personnel vice minister Yin Kaishan, grand herald Liu Shilong, Court of Imperial Sacrifices vice minister Liu Zhenghui, director of waterways Zhao Wenke, storehouse bureau director Wu Shihuo, cavalry general Zhang Pinggao, Li Sixing, Li Gaoqian, Left Garrison Guard office chief administrator Xu Shixu, and fourteen others in all were granted pardon for one capital offense.

sentences.zh: 武德九年十月，太宗又定功臣封戶，時文靜已死，乃自寂而下差功大小第之，總四十三人。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the ninth year of Wude, Taizong again fixed the fief households of the merit subjects. Wenjing was already dead, so from Ji downward they were ranked by degree of merit, forty-three men in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the ninth year of Wude, Emperor Taizong again fixed the fief households of the merit subjects. Liu Wenjing was already dead, so from Pei Ji downward they were ranked by merit, forty-three men in all.

sentences.zh: 寂戶千五百，長孫無忌、王君廓、尉遲敬德、房玄齡、杜如晦戶千三百，長孫順德、柴紹、羅藝、趙郡王孝恭戶千二百，侯君集、張公謹、劉師立戶千，李勣、劉弘基戶九百，高士廉、宇文士及、秦叔寶、程知節戶七百，安興貴、安修仁、唐儉、竇軌、屈突通、蕭瑀、封德彜、劉義節戶六百，錢九隴、樊興、公孫武達、李孟嘗、段誌玄、龐卿惲、張亮、李藥師、杜淹、元仲文戶四百，張長遜、張平高、李安遠、李子和、秦行師、馬三寶戶三百。

translations.literal: Ji's households were fifteen hundred; Zhangsun Wuji, Wang Junkuo, Yuchi Jingde, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui thirteen hundred each; Zhangsun Shunde, Chai Shao, Luo Yi, and Prince Zhao of Zhao Commandery Xiaogong twelve hundred each; Hou Junji, Zhang Gongjin, and Liu Shili one thousand each; Li Ji and Liu Hongji nine hundred each; Gao Shilian, Yuwen Shiji, Qin Shubao, and Cheng Zhijie seven hundred each; An Xinggui, An Xiuren, Tang Jian, Dou Gui, Qu Tuotong, Xiao Yu, Feng Deyi, and Liu Yijie six hundred each; Qian Jiulong, Fan Xing, Gongsun Wuda, Li Mengchang, Duan Zhixuan, Pang Qingyun, Zhang Liang, Li Yaoshi, Du Yan, and Yuan Zhongwen four hundred each; Zhang Changsun, Zhang Pinggao, Li Anyuan, Li Zihe, Qin Xingshi, and Ma Sanbao three hundred each.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji received fifteen hundred households; Zhangsun Wuji, Wang Junkuo, Yuchi Jingde, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui thirteen hundred each; Zhangsun Shunde, Chai Shao, Luo Yi, and Prince Zhao of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong twelve hundred each; Hou Junji, Zhang Gongjin, and Liu Shili one thousand each; Li Ji and Liu Hongji nine hundred each; Gao Shilian, Yuwen Shiji, Qin Shubao, and Cheng Zhijie seven hundred each; An Xinggui, An Xiuren, Tang Jian, Dou Gui, Qu Tuotong, Xiao Yu, Feng Deyi, and Liu Yijie six hundred each; Qian Jiulong, Fan Xing, Gongsun Wuda, Li Mengchang, Duan Zhixuan, Pang Qingyun, Zhang Liang, Li Yaoshi, Du Yan, and Yuan Zhongwen four hundred each; and Zhang Changsun, Zhang Pinggao, Li Anyuan, Li Zihe, Qin Xingshi, and Ma Sanbao three hundred each.

sentences.zh: 寂等三十人已見於傳。

translations.literal: Thirty of Ji and the others have already appeared in their biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty of these men, including Pei Ji, already appear in their own biographies.

sentences.zh: 自趙文恪等十八人功不甚顯，然參附義始事，班班見當世。

translations.literal: From Zhao Wenke and eighteen others, though their merit was not very prominent, they nonetheless joined at the beginning in supporting the righteous undertaking, and their names are clearly visible in their own age.
translations.idiomatic: As for Zhao Wenke and eighteen others, though their merit was not especially conspicuous, they nonetheless joined the righteous cause at the outset, and their names were well known in their day.

sentences.zh: 今次第其名，總出左方雲。

translations.literal: Now their names are listed in order, all set forth at left below.
translations.idiomatic: Their names are now listed in order below.

sentences.zh: 趙文恪，并州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Wenke was a native of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenke was a native of Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為隋鷹揚府司馬。

translations.literal: He served as Marshal of the Hawkish Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He served as marshal of a hawkish garrison under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 義兵起，授右三統軍。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, he was appointed Right Third Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose, he was appointed Right Third Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，擢都水監，封新興郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude he was promoted to Director of Waterways and enfeoffed as Duke of Xinxing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wude he was promoted to director of waterways and enfeoffed as Duke of Xinxing Commandery.

sentences.zh: 時中國經大亂，馬耗，會突厥講和，詔文恪至并州，與齊王誘市邊馬以備軍。

translations.literal: At that time the central realm had suffered great disorder and horses were depleted. When peace was made with the Turks, Wenke was ordered to go to Bing Prefecture and, with the Prince of Qi, entice border markets to sell horses for military use.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the realm had been ravaged by chaos and horses were scarce. When peace was made with the Turks, Wenke was ordered to go to Bing Prefecture and, together with the Prince of Qi, purchase border horses for the army.

sentences.zh: 劉武周寇太原，屬城盡沒，李仲文守浩州，兵力孤絕，齊王使文恪率步騎千余助守。

translations.literal: Liu Wuzhou raided Taiyuan and the subordinate cities were all lost. Li Zhongwen held Hao Prefecture with isolated, exhausted forces; the Prince of Qi sent Wenke with more than a thousand foot and horse to assist in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuzhou invaded Taiyuan, every subordinate city fell. Li Zhongwen held Hao Prefecture with isolated, exhausted forces, and the Prince of Qi sent Wenke with more than a thousand infantry and cavalry to help defend it.

sentences.zh: 會太原陷，遂棄城遁，詔下獄死。

translations.literal: When Taiyuan fell he abandoned the city and fled. An edict ordered him imprisoned and executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiyuan fell he abandoned the city and fled. An edict ordered him imprisoned and put to death.

sentences.zh: 李思行，趙州人，避仇太原。

translations.literal: Li Sixing was a native of Zhao Prefecture and had fled to Taiyuan to escape a blood feud.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sixing was a native of Zhao Prefecture who had fled to Taiyuan to escape a blood feud.

sentences.zh: 唐公將起，使覘訁冋長安，還，具論機策，以贊大議授左三統軍。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Tang was about to rise, he was sent to reconnoiter Chang'an. On his return he fully set forth stratagems and, to support the great plan, was appointed Left Third Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Tang was preparing to rise, he was sent to reconnoiter Chang'an. On his return he laid out the whole strategic situation and, for supporting the great plan, was appointed Left Third Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 從破霍邑，平京師，擢累嘉州刺史、樂安郡公。

translations.literal: He followed in breaking Huoyi and pacifying the capital, was promoted through successive ranks to Governor of Jia Prefecture and Duke of Le'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the army in breaking Huoyi and pacifying the capital, and was promoted through successive ranks to governor of Jia Prefecture and Duke of Le'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈洪州都督，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was granted Governor-General of Hong Prefecture, with posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the title of governor-general of Hong Prefecture, with the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 李高遷，岐州人，客太原，唐公引致左右。

translations.literal: Li Gaoqian was a native of Qi Prefecture, a guest at Taiyuan whom the Duke of Tang drew to his side.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gaoqian was a native of Qi Prefecture who had been living as a guest at Taiyuan when the Duke of Tang drew him to his side.

sentences.zh: 執高君雅等有功，以右三統軍從下霍邑，圍長安，力戰。

translations.literal: For arresting Gao Junya and others with merit, he followed as Right Third Commander-in-Chief in taking Huoyi, besieging Chang'an, and fighting fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in arresting Gao Junya and others, he served as Right Third Commander-in-Chief in the capture of Huoyi, the siege of Chang'an, and fierce combat.

sentences.zh: 遷左武衛大將軍、江夏郡公、檢校西麟州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Martial Guard, Duke of Jiangxia Commandery, and Acting Governor of Western Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the Left Martial Guard, made Duke of Jiangxia Commandery, and appointed acting governor of Western Lin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 突厥寇馬邑，高滿政請救，詔高遷督兵助守。

translations.literal: When the Turks raided Mayi, Gao Manzheng requested relief; an edict ordered Gaoqian to lead troops to assist in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided Mayi, Gao Manzheng requested relief, and an edict ordered Gaoqian to lead troops to help defend the city.

sentences.zh: 賊盛，乃夜斬關走，所將皆沒，坐除名徙邊。

translations.literal: The bandits were strong; he cut through the gate by night and fled, and all the men he led were lost. He was punished by removal from the registers and exile to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy was too strong. He broke through the gate by night and fled, and all the men under his command were lost. He was stripped of rank and exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 後歷資州刺史，卒，贈涼州都督。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as Governor of Zi Prefecture; he died and was posthumously granted Governor-General of Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as governor of Zi Prefecture, died in office, and was posthumously granted the title of governor-general of Liang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 姜寶誼，秦州上邽人。

translations.literal: Jiang Baoyi was a native of Shanggui in Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Baoyi was a native of Shanggui in Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父遠，仁周為秦州刺史、朝邑縣公。

translations.literal: His father Yuan, under Northern Zhou, was Governor of Qin Prefecture and Duke of Chaoyi County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan had served Northern Zhou as governor of Qin Prefecture and Duke of Chaoyi County.

sentences.zh: 寶誼遊太學，受書，業不進，去為左翊衛，以積勞遷鷹揚郎將，領府兵，從高祖督盜太原。

translations.literal: Baoyi studied at the Imperial Academy but made no progress in his learning; he left and became a Left Flank Guard officer, and through accumulated merit was transferred to Hawkish Commandant, commanding garrison troops and following Gaozu in suppressing bandits at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyi studied at the Imperial Academy but made little progress and left to join the Left Flank Guard. Through accumulated service he rose to hawkish commandant, commanding garrison troops, and followed Emperor Gaozu in suppressing bandits at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 及起兵，授左統軍，下西河、霍邑，以多，爵累永安縣公，歷右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When the army rose he was appointed Left Commander-in-Chief, took Xihe and Huoyi, and for his many merits was enfeoffed successively as Duke of Yong'an County; he served as General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the army rose he was appointed Left Commander-in-Chief, captured Xihe and Huoyi, and for his many merits was enfeoffed as Duke of Yong'an County and later served as general of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 劉武周使黃子英數盜雀鼠谷，帝遣寶誼擊之。

translations.literal: Liu Wuzhou sent Huang Ziying repeatedly to plunder Que-Shu Valley; the emperor sent Baoyi to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou sent Huang Ziying to raid Que-Shu Valley again and again, and the emperor sent Baoyi to repel him.

sentences.zh: 賊輕甲挑師，戰接而三遁，逐之，伏發，寶誼為賊執，俄亡歸。

translations.literal: The bandits in light armor provoked battle; after contact they feigned retreat three times, and when pursued an ambush was sprung. Baoyi was seized by the bandits but soon escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy in light armor provoked battle, then feigned retreat three times during the engagement. When Baoyi pursued, an ambush sprang up and he was captured by the rebels, though he soon escaped and returned.

sentences.zh: 與裴寂拒宋金剛，戰汾州，兵合，寂棄軍走，寶誼復為所禽。

translations.literal: With Pei Ji he resisted Song Jingang and fought at Fen Prefecture. When the armies joined, Ji abandoned the army and fled, and Baoyi was again captured.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Pei Ji he resisted Song Jingang and fought at Fen Prefecture. When the armies joined battle, Pei Ji abandoned his troops and fled, and Baoyi was captured again.

sentences.zh: 帝聞為泣下曰：「彼烈士，必不下賊，死矣！

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he wept and said: "That resolute warrior will surely not submit to the bandits—he is dead!
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he wept and said, "That resolute warrior would never submit to the enemy—he must be dead!

sentences.zh: 「賜其家物千段，米三百斛。

translations.literal: " He granted his household a thousand bolts of goods and three hundred hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: " He granted Baoyi's family a thousand bolts of goods and three hundred hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 果謀還，被害。

translations.literal: As expected, he plotted to return and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: As expected, Baoyi plotted to escape and was killed.

sentences.zh: 且死，西向大呼曰：「臣無狀，負陛下。

translations.literal: As he was about to die, he shouted toward the west: "Your servant is worthless—I have failed Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of death he shouted toward the west, "Your servant is unworthy—I have failed Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」賊平，詔迎其柩，贈左衛大將軍、幽州總管，謚曰剛。

translations.literal: " When the bandits were pacified, an edict ordered his coffin escorted back; posthumously he was granted General of the Left Guard and Governor-General of You Prefecture, with posthumous title Gang.
translations.idiomatic: " After the rebels were pacified, an edict ordered his coffin escorted home. He was posthumously granted the titles of general of the Left Guard and governor-general of You Prefecture, with the posthumous name Gang.

sentences.zh: 子協，字壽，善篆籀。

translations.literal: His son Xie, courtesy name Shou, was skilled in seal and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xie, courtesy name Shou, was skilled in seal and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 歷燕然都護、夏州都督，封成紀縣侯，謚曰威。

translations.literal: He served successively as Protector-General of Yanshan and Governor-General of Xia Prefecture, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chengji County, with posthumous title Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as protector-general of Yanshan and governor-general of Xia Prefecture, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chengji County, and received the posthumous name Wei.

sentences.zh: 許世緒，并州人。

translations.literal: Xu Shixu was a native of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shixu was a native of Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋鷹揚府司馬。

translations.literal: He was Marshal of the Hawkish Garrison under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He served as marshal of a hawkish garrison under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 知隋將亡，請唐公曰：「天輔德，人與能，乘機不發，後必蹈悔。

translations.literal: Seeing that the Sui would perish, he said to the Duke of Tang: "Heaven assists the virtuous, and the people grant capacity. If one does not seize the moment and act, afterward one must tread regret.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the Sui dynasty was doomed, he said to the Duke of Tang, "Heaven assists the virtuous, and the people grant them power. Fail to act on this moment, and regret will follow.

sentences.zh: 隋政不綱，天下搖亂，公姓名已著謠箓，今攬五郡之兵，據四戰之沖，茍無奇計，禍不反踵。

translations.literal: Sui governance lacks restraint; the realm shakes in disorder. Your name is already marked in prophecy and registers. Now you hold the armies of five commanderies and occupy a crossroads of four-way battle—if you have no extraordinary plan, disaster will overtake you before you can turn.
translations.idiomatic: Sui governance has lost all restraint and the realm trembles in chaos. Your name already appears in prophecy and popular lore. You now command the armies of five commanderies and hold a crossroads where every power must fight. Without a bold plan, disaster will overtake you before you can turn around.

sentences.zh: 若收取英俊，為天下倡，帝王業也。

translations.literal: If you gather the outstanding and take the lead for the realm, that is the enterprise of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: If you gather the outstanding men of the realm and lead the cause of righteousness, you will found an imperial enterprise.

sentences.zh: 」公奇之，顧倚親密。

translations.literal: " The duke marveled at him and relied on him with intimate trust.
translations.idiomatic: " The Duke of Tang was impressed and came to rely on him as a close confidant.

sentences.zh: 兵起，授右一府司馬。

translations.literal: When the army rose he was appointed Right First Office Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When the army rose he was appointed marshal of the Right First Office.

sentences.zh: 累除蔡州刺史、真定郡公，卒。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he became governor of Cai Prefecture and Marquis of Zhending Commandery, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to governor of Cai Prefecture and Marquis of Zhending Commandery, then died.

sentences.zh: 弟洛仁，亦從起晉陽，錄功至冠軍大將軍。

translations.literal: His younger brother Luoren also rose from Jinyang; for recorded merit he reached Champion Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Luoren also joined the rising at Jinyang and, for recorded merit, rose to Champion Grand General.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈代州都督，謚曰勇，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Protector-General of Dai Prefecture, with posthumous name Yong, and buried with Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Protector-General of Dai Prefecture, given the posthumous name Yong, and granted burial at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 劉師立，宋州虞城人。

translations.literal: Liu Shili was a native of Yucheng in Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shili was a native of Yucheng in Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 始事王世充為親將，洛陽平，當誅，秦王壯其才，釋不死，引為左親衛。

translations.literal: He first served Wang Shichong as a trusted general. When Luoyang fell he should have been executed, but the Prince of Qin admired his talent, spared him, and brought him in as Left Personal Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He had first served Wang Shichong as a trusted general. When Luoyang fell he was marked for execution, but the Prince of Qin admired his talent, spared his life, and took him on as a member of the Left Personal Guard.

sentences.zh: 建成之釁，師立參奉密議，後與尉遲敬德、龐卿惲、李孟嘗等九人錄功拜左衛率。

translations.literal: At the crisis over Crown Prince Jiancheng, Shili took part in secret deliberations; afterward, with Yuchi Jingde, Pang Qingyun, Li Mengchang, and eight others, he was recorded for merit and appointed Left Guard Commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the crisis over Crown Prince Jiancheng, Shili took part in the secret deliberations. Later he and Yuchi Jingde, Pang Qingyun, Li Mengchang, and six others were rewarded for merit and appointed Left Guard Commander.

sentences.zh: 遷左驍衛將軍、襄武郡公，賜絹五千匹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Xiao Guard General and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangwu Commandery, and granted five thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Xiao Guard General and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangwu Commandery, with a gift of five thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 有告師立姓在符讖欲反者，太宗謂曰：「人言卿將反，果乎？

translations.literal: Someone reported that Shili's surname appeared in prophecy and that he intended rebellion. Taizong said to him: "People say you will rebel—is it so?
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Shili's surname appeared in prophetic texts and that he planned rebellion. Taizong said to him, "People say you mean to rebel. Is it true?

sentences.zh: 」師立對曰：「臣為隋官，不過六品，材駑下，不敢希富貴。

translations.literal: " Shili replied: "Your subject served the Sui as an official of no more than sixth rank; my talent is dull and low—I dared not hope for wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: " Shili replied, "Your subject served the Sui as an official of no more than sixth rank. My talent is modest, and I never dared hope for wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 今遭非常之會，位將軍，顧巳極矣，何敢反？

translations.literal: Now I have met an extraordinary occasion and hold the rank of general—looking back, this is already the utmost. How would I dare rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Now I have met with extraordinary fortune and hold the rank of general. Looking back, I have already reached the limit of what I could hope for. How could I dare rebel?

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「朕知妄耳！

translations.literal: " The emperor laughed and said: "I know it is false!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed and said, "I know it is nonsense!

sentences.zh: 」賜束帛，召入臥內慰勉。

translations.literal: " He granted bolts of silk and summoned him into the inner chamber to comfort and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: " He granted him bolts of silk and summoned him into the inner chamber to comfort and encourage him.

sentences.zh: 羅藝反，京師震駭，詔師立檢校右武候大將軍，勒兵備非常。

translations.literal: When Luo Yi rebelled the capital was shaken in alarm; an edict appointed Shili acting Right Martial Guard Grand General and ordered troops drawn up against emergency.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Yi rebelled, the capital was shaken with alarm. An edict appointed Shili acting Right Martial Guard Grand General and ordered him to muster troops against any emergency.

sentences.zh: 藝平，有司劾黨與，師立坐與善，除名。

translations.literal: When Luo Yi was pacified, the authorities impeached his associates; Shili was convicted of friendly association and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: After Luo Yi was suppressed, the authorities impeached his associates. Shili was convicted of having been on friendly terms with him and was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 尋以籓邸舊，檢校岐州都督。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of old ties to the princely residence, he was appointed acting Protector-General of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on account of his old ties to the princely residence, he was appointed acting Protector-General of Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上書請討吐谷渾，未報，即遣使間諭部落，多降附者，列其地為開、橋二州。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting a campaign against Tuyuhun. Before reply came, he sent envoys to persuade the tribes in secret; many submitted, and their lands were set up as Kai and Qiao Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial requesting a campaign against Tuyuhun. Before any reply arrived, he sent envoys to win over the tribes in secret. Many submitted, and their lands were organized as Kai and Qiao Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 又党項酋拓拔赤辭先附吐谷渾，倚險自守，亦遣說下之，詔赤辭為西戎州都督。

translations.literal: Also, the Tangut chieftain Tuo Ba Chici had first submitted to Tuyuhun and, relying on rugged terrain, held himself in defense. Shili likewise sent persuaders and won him over; an edict made Chici Protector-General of Xirong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut chieftain Tuo Ba Chici had first submitted to Tuyuhun and, relying on rugged terrain, held out in defense. Shili likewise sent persuaders and won him over, and an edict appointed Chici Protector-General of Xirong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 師立以母喪解，岐人表留，遂不得赴哀。

translations.literal: Shili resigned on account of his mother's death, but the people of Qi submitted a memorial to retain him, and so he could not go to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: Shili resigned on account of his mother's death, but the people of Qi submitted a memorial asking that he remain, and so he was unable to go and mourn.

sentences.zh: 時河西党項破醜氏嘗苦邊，又阻新附，師立討之。

translations.literal: At that time the Tangut Pochou clan west of the river had long harassed the frontier and now obstructed the newly submitted; Shili campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Tangut Pochou clan west of the river had long harassed the frontier and now obstructed the newly submitted peoples, so Shili campaigned against them.

sentences.zh: 軍未至，破醜懼，遁去，師立窮追之，抵恤於真山而還。

translations.literal: Before the army arrived, the Pochou were afraid and fled. Shili pursued them to the end, reaching Xu at Zhen Mountain, then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army arrived, the Pochou were frightened and fled. Shili pursued them relentlessly as far as Xu at Zhen Mountain, then returned.

sentences.zh: 又戰吐谷渾於小莫門川，破之。

translations.literal: He again fought Tuyuhun at Xiaomomen River and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He again fought Tuyuhun at Xiaomomen River and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 轉始州刺史，卒，謚曰肅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor of Shi Prefecture, died, and received posthumous name Su.
