translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Shi Prefecture, died, and was given the posthumous name Su.

sentences.zh: 劉義節，并州人。

translations.literal: Liu Yijie was a native of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijie was a native of Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，補晉陽鄉長，富於財。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui Daye era he was appointed district chief of Jinyang and was rich in wealth.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui Daye era he was appointed district chief of Jinyang and was a man of considerable wealth.

sentences.zh: 裴寂薦之唐公，又與王威、高君雅遊，然於唐公為最厚。

translations.literal: Pei Ji recommended him to the Duke of Tang. He also associated with Wang Wei and Gao Junya, yet with the Duke of Tang his ties were closest.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji recommended him to the Duke of Tang. He also kept company with Wang Wei and Gao Junya, but his ties with the Duke of Tang were the closest of all.

sentences.zh: 兵將起，威、君雅疑之，義節刺知其情，得先事禽威等。

translations.literal: When the army was about to rise, Wei and Junya grew suspicious. Yijie secretly learned their intentions and was able to act first and seize Wei and the others.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was about to rise, Wei and Junya grew suspicious. Yijie secretly learned their intentions and was able to act first and seize Wei and the others.

sentences.zh: 從平京師，為鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying the capital and became Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in pacifying the capital and was appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時傾府庫為軍賞，帑財大乏。

translations.literal: At the time the treasury was emptied for military rewards, and state funds were greatly depleted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the treasury was being emptied for military rewards, and state funds were severely depleted.

sentences.zh: 義節曰：「今京師屯兵多，樵貴帛賤，若伐街苑樹為薪，以易布帛，歲數十萬可致。

translations.literal: Yijie said: "Now many troops are stationed in the capital; firewood is costly and cloth cheap. If we cut the trees of the streets and parks for fuel and exchange them for cloth, several hundred thousand can be obtained in a year.
translations.idiomatic: Yijie said, "Many troops are now stationed in the capital, firewood is costly and cloth is cheap. If we cut the trees of the streets and parks for fuel and exchange them for cloth, we can obtain several hundred thousand [strings of cash] in a year.

sentences.zh: 」又請軸舒藏內見繒，取羨尺，補雜費，得十余萬段，調度遂給。

translations.literal: " He also requested to unroll the silk stored within the treasury, take the surplus lengths, and apply them to miscellaneous expenses, obtaining more than a hundred thousand bolts, so that supply and allocation were finally sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked to unroll the silk stored in the treasury, take the surplus lengths for miscellaneous expenses, and thereby obtain more than a hundred thousand bolts, so that supplies were finally sufficient.

sentences.zh: 遷太府，封葛國公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Court of the Imperial Treasury and enfeoffed as Duke of Ge.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Court of the Imperial Treasury and enfeoffed as Duke of Ge.

sentences.zh: 義節本名世龍，或言世龍子名鳳昌，父子非人臣兆，高祖不聽，更賜今名。

translations.literal: Yijie's original name was Shilong. Some said that Shilong's son was named Fengchang, and that father and son bore signs unbecoming a subject. Gaozu would not heed this and instead granted his present name.
translations.idiomatic: Yijie's original name was Shilong. Some said that Shilong's son was named Fengchang and that father and son bore omens unbecoming a subject. Gaozu would not heed this and instead granted him his present name.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，轉少府監，坐貴入賈人珠及故出署丞罪，廢為民，徙嶺南，終欽州別駕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was transferred to Director of the Palace Workshops. He was convicted of selling pearls to merchants at high price and of the offense of releasing a bureau assistant, was degraded to commoner status, exiled to Lingnan, and ended as assistant administrator of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he was transferred to Director of the Palace Workshops. He was convicted of selling pearls to merchants at inflated prices and of improperly releasing a bureau assistant, was degraded to commoner status, exiled to Lingnan, and ended his career as assistant administrator of Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從子思禮，武後時為箕州刺史。

translations.literal: His nephew Sil, under Empress Wu, served as governor of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Liu Sil served as governor of Ji Prefecture under Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 少學相人於張憬藏，憬藏謂思禮歷刺史，位至太師。

translations.literal: In youth he studied physiognomy under Zhang Jingzang, who told Sil he would pass through governorships and reach Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied physiognomy under Zhang Jingzang, who told Sil that he would serve as governor in succession and rise to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天二年，授箕州，益喜，以為太師位尊，非佐命不可得，乃結洛州錄事參軍綦連耀謀反，謂耀曰；

translations.literal: In the second year of Wansui Tongtian he was appointed to Ji Prefecture and grew still more pleased, thinking that the rank of Grand Preceptor was exalted and could not be obtained except by one who aided the Mandate; he then joined Luozhou Registrar Qilian Yao in plotting rebellion and said to Yao:
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wansui Tongtian he was appointed to Ji Prefecture and grew still more pleased, believing that the rank of Grand Preceptor was so exalted it could be attained only by one who had aided the Mandate. He then joined Luozhou Registrar Qilian Yao in plotting rebellion and said to Yao:

sentences.zh: 「君體有龍氣如大帝。

translations.literal: "Your body bears dragon qi like the Great Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: "Your body bears the dragon aura of a great emperor.

sentences.zh: 」耀亦曰：「公金刀，當輔我。

translations.literal: " Yao also said: "Your Excellency bears the surname Jin Dao—you should assist me.
translations.idiomatic: " Yao also said, "Your Excellency bears the surname Liu—you should assist me.

sentences.zh: 」陰約君臣。

translations.literal: " In secret they bound themselves as sovereign and minister.
translations.idiomatic: " In secret they bound themselves in the roles of sovereign and minister.

sentences.zh: 思禮因以術眩眾，見者必曰：「當三品」，使嗜進者充望，然後云：「綦連耀且受命，公等皆因之。

translations.literal: Sil then used his arts to dazzle the crowd; to every visitor he would say, "You will reach third rank," filling those eager for advancement with expectation, and then say, "Qilian Yao is about to receive the Mandate—you all will rise through him.
translations.idiomatic: Sil then used his arts to dazzle the crowd. To every visitor he would say, "You will reach third rank," filling those eager for advancement with expectation, and then declare, "Qilian Yao is about to receive the Mandate—you will all rise through him.

sentences.zh: 事敗，武懿宗按之，陰弛思禮禁，使多逮引。

translations.literal: When the affair failed, Wu Yizong investigated it, secretly loosening Sil's restraints so that he might implicate many others.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot failed, Wu Yizong investigated the case and secretly loosened Sil's restraints so that he might implicate as many others as possible.

sentences.zh: 思禮冀自脫，悉引素相忤者，將刑猶不寤，與眾人斬於市。

translations.literal: Sil hoped to save himself and implicated all who had long been at odds with him. Even as execution approached he still did not awaken, and was beheaded in the marketplace with the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Sil hoped to save himself and implicated all who had long been at odds with him. Even as execution approached he still did not understand what he had done, and was beheaded in the marketplace along with the others.

sentences.zh: 其知名者，如李元素、孫元亨、石抱忠、王抃、抃兄勔、路敬淳等三十余族，竄逐千余人。

translations.literal: Among the well-known were more than thirty clans, such as Li Yuansu, Sun Yuanheng, Shi Baozhong, Wang Bian, Bian's elder brother Min, and Lu Jingchun; more than a thousand people were banished.
translations.idiomatic: Among the well-known victims were more than thirty clans, including Li Yuansu, Sun Yuanheng, Shi Baozhong, Wang Bian, Bian's elder brother Min, and Lu Jingchun; more than a thousand people were banished in the purge.

sentences.zh: 錢九隴，字永業，湖州長城人。

translations.literal: Qian Jiulong, courtesy name Yongye, was a native of Changcheng in Hu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Jiulong, courtesy name Yongye, was a native of Changcheng in Hu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父文強，為吳明徹裨將，與明徹俱敗彭城。

translations.literal: His father Wenqiang was a lieutenant general under Wu Mingche and was defeated with Mingche at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenqiang was a lieutenant general under Wu Mingche and was defeated with Mingche at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 入隋，以罪沒為奴，故九隴事唐公。

translations.literal: Entering the Sui, he was enslaved for a crime; hence Jiulong served the Duke of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: After entering the Sui dynasty he was enslaved for a crime, and so Jiulong came to serve the Duke of Tang.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，常備左右。

translations.literal: Skilled in horsemanship and archery, he was constantly on duty at the side.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in horsemanship and archery, he was constantly on duty at the Duke's side.

sentences.zh: 兵起，以功授金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the army rose he was granted Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon for merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the army rose he was granted the title Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon for his merit.

sentences.zh: 從戰薛仁杲、劉武周，擢累為右武衛將軍。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigns against Xue Rengao and Liu Wuzhou and was repeatedly promoted to Right Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in campaigns against Xue Rengao and Liu Wuzhou and was repeatedly promoted until he reached Right Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 從平洛陽，佐皇太子建成討劉黑闥魏州，力戰破賊，以功最封郇國公，以本官為苑遊將軍。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Luoyang and assisted Crown Prince Jiancheng in campaigning against Liu Heita at Wei Prefecture; fighting hard he broke the rebels. For highest merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xun and retained his original office as Park Excursion General.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in pacifying Luoyang and assisted Crown Prince Jiancheng in campaigning against Liu Heita at Wei Prefecture. Fighting hard, he broke the rebels, and for the highest merit was enfeoffed as Duke of Xun while retaining his original office as Park Excursion General.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，為眉州刺史，改巢國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he became governor of Mei Prefecture and his fief was changed to Chao.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he became governor of Mei Prefecture, and his fief was changed to Chao.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左武衛大將軍、潭州都督，謚曰勇，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Left Martial Guard Grand General and Protector-General of Tan Prefecture, with posthumous name Yong, and buried with Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Left Martial Guard Grand General and Protector-General of Tan Prefecture, given the posthumous name Yong, and granted burial at Xianling.

sentences.zh: 樊興，安州人。

translations.literal: Fan Xing was a native of An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xing was a native of An Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以罪為奴。

translations.literal: For a crime he became a slave.
translations.idiomatic: He had been enslaved for a crime.

sentences.zh: 從唐公平長安，授左監門將軍。

translations.literal: He followed the Duke of Tang in pacifying Chang'an and was appointed Left Gate Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Duke of Tang in pacifying Chang'an and was appointed Left Gate Guard General.

sentences.zh: 從秦王積戰多，封營國公，數賜黃金雜物。

translations.literal: Following the Prince of Qin he accumulated many battles and was enfeoffed as Duke of Ying; gold and various goods were repeatedly granted him.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Prince of Qin he fought in many battles, was enfeoffed as Duke of Ying, and was repeatedly granted gold and other valuables.

sentences.zh: 後坐事削爵。

translations.literal: Later he was convicted of an offense and his title was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was convicted of an offense and stripped of his title.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，陵州獠反，命討之，為左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan the Liao of Ling Prefecture rebelled; he was ordered to campaign against them and became Left Xiao Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenguan the Liao of Ling Prefecture rebelled. He was ordered to campaign against them and was appointed Left Xiao Guard General.

sentences.zh: 又從李靖擊吐谷渾，為赤水道行軍總管。

translations.literal: He again followed Li Jing in attacking Tuyuhun and served as Campaign Commander of the Chishui Route.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Li Jing in attacking Tuyuhun and served as Campaign Commander of the Chishui Route.

sentences.zh: 後軍期，士多死，亡失器仗，以勛減死。

translations.literal: Later he missed the army's deadline; many soldiers died and weapons were lost. For his merit his death sentence was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Later he missed the army's deadline; many soldiers died and weapons were lost. On account of his past merit his death sentence was commuted.

sentences.zh: 後為左監門大將軍、襄城郡公。

translations.literal: Later he became Left Gate Guard Grand General and Duke of Xiangcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Left Gate Guard Grand General and Duke of Xiangcheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 太宗征遼，以興忠謹，副房玄齡留守京師，檢校右武候將軍。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned against Liaodong, Xing was appointed for loyalty and prudence to assist Fang Xuanling in holding the capital and served as acting Right Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong campaigned against Liaodong, Xing was chosen for his loyalty and prudence to assist Fang Xuanling in holding the capital and served as acting Right Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左武候大將軍、洪州都督，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Left Martial Guard Grand General and Protector-General of Hong Prefecture, and buried with Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Left Martial Guard Grand General and Protector-General of Hong Prefecture, and granted burial at Xianling.

sentences.zh: 公孫武達，京兆櫟陽人。

translations.literal: Gongsun Wuda was a native of Liyang in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Wuda was a native of Liyang in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 以豪俠稱，為隋驍果。

translations.literal: Known for bold chivalry, he was a Sui elite guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: Known for bold chivalry, he served as a Sui elite guardsman.

sentences.zh: 兵興，武達至長春宮上謁。

translations.literal: When the army rose, Wuda went to Changchun Palace to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: When the army rose, Wuda went to Changchun Palace to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 從秦王討劉武周，苦戰功多，累遷秦府右三軍驃騎，封清水縣公。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Qin in campaigning against Liu Wuzhou; through bitter fighting his merit was great, and he was repeatedly promoted to Qin Prince's Residence Right Third Army Cavalry General and enfeoffed as Duke of Qingshui County.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Qin in campaigning against Liu Wuzhou. Through bitter fighting he won great merit and was repeatedly promoted to Cavalry General of the Right Third Army in the Qin Prince's Residence, and enfeoffed as Duke of Qingshui County.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，為肅州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he became governor of Su Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he became governor of Su Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 突厥騎數千、輜重萬余入寇，謀南趨吐谷渾，武達以精兵二千人與戰，虜稍卻，復殊死鬥，薄之張掖河，潛命上流度兵，虜已半濟，乃兩岸夾擊，斬溺略盡。

translations.literal: Several thousand Turkic horsemen and more than ten thousand loads of baggage entered to raid, planning to drive south toward Tuyuhun. Wuda fought them with two thousand elite troops; the enemy slightly withdrew, then fought to the death again. Pressing them to the Zhangye River, he secretly ordered troops to cross upstream. When the enemy were half across, he struck from both banks and killed or drowned nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand Turkic horsemen and more than ten thousand loads of baggage raided the frontier, planning to drive south toward Tuyuhun. Wuda met them with two thousand elite troops. The enemy fell back slightly, then fought again to the death. Pressing them to the Zhangye River, he secretly ordered troops to cross upstream. When the enemy were half across the river, he struck from both banks and killed or drowned nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 璽書勞之，遷左監門將軍。

translations.literal: An imperial letter commended him, and he was transferred to Left Gate Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial letter commended him, and he was transferred to Left Gate Guard General.

sentences.zh: 鹽州突厥叛，詔武達趨靈州，追及賊，賊方度河，乃據南涯陣，武達擊之，斬其帥可邏拔扈，進封東萊郡公。

translations.literal: When the Turks of Yan Prefecture rebelled, an edict ordered Wuda to hurry to Ling Prefecture. He overtook the rebels as they were crossing the river, took position on the south bank, and struck them, beheading their leader Keluobahu. He was advanced to Duke of Donglai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks of Yan Prefecture rebelled, an edict ordered Wuda to hurry to Ling Prefecture. He overtook the rebels as they were crossing the river, took position on the south bank, and attacked, beheading their leader Keluobahu. He was promoted to Duke of Donglai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 終右武衛大將軍，贈荊州都督，陪葬昭陵，謚曰壯。

translations.literal: He ended as Right Martial Guard Grand General, was posthumously granted Protector-General of Jing Prefecture, buried with Zhaoling, and received posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Right Martial Guard Grand General, was posthumously made Protector-General of Jing Prefecture, granted burial at Zhaoling, and given the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 龐卿惲，并州人。

translations.literal: Pang Qingyun was a native of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Qingyun was a native of Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從討隱太子有功，拜右驍衛將軍、邾國公。

translations.literal: He followed in suppressing the Hidden Crown Prince with merit and was appointed Right Xiao Guard General and Duke of Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in suppressing the Hidden Crown Prince with merit and was appointed Right Xiao Guard General and Duke of Zhu.

sentences.zh: 卒，追改濮國。

translations.literal: He died, and posthumously his fief was changed to Pu.
translations.idiomatic: He died, and posthumously his fief was changed to Pu.

sentences.zh: 子同善，右金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: His son Tongshan was Right Golden Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tongshan served as Right Golden Guard Grand General.

sentences.zh: 同善子承宗，開元初，仕至太子賓客。

translations.literal: Tongshan's son Chengzong, at the beginning of Kaiyuan, served until reaching Crown Prince's Guest.
translations.idiomatic: Tongshan's son Chengzong, at the beginning of the Kaiyuan era, rose to serve as Guest of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 張長遜，京兆櫟陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Changsun was a native of Liyang in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changsun was a native of Liyang in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 精馳射，在隋為裏長。

translations.literal: Skilled in mounted archery, under the Sui he was a village chief.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in mounted archery, he served under the Sui as a village chief.

sentences.zh: 以平陳功，擢上開府，累遷五原郡通守。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying Chen he was promoted to Senior Opening Grand Master and was repeatedly transferred until he became Administrator of Wuyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in pacifying Chen he was promoted to Senior Opening Grand Master and rose through successive appointments to Administrator of Wuyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 遭亂，附突厥，突厥號為割利特勒。

translations.literal: When disorder struck he submitted to the Turks, who styled him Gelitele.
translations.idiomatic: When disorder struck he submitted to the Turks, who styled him Gelitele.

sentences.zh: 義兵起，以郡降，即拜五原太守、安化郡公，徙封范陽。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose he surrendered the commandery and was immediately appointed Administrator of Wuyuan and Duke of Anhua Commandery; his fief was moved to Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose he surrendered the commandery and was immediately appointed Administrator of Wuyuan and Duke of Anhua Commandery, with his fief moved to Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 時梁師都、薛舉請突厥兵南度河，長遜矯作詔與莫賀咄設，以伐其謀，會唐使亦至，突厥兵不出。

translations.literal: At the time Liang Shidu and Xue Ju requested Turkic troops to cross the river south. Changsun forged an edict to Mohuaduo She to thwart their plot; as it happened a Tang envoy also arrived, and the Turkic troops did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liang Shidu and Xue Ju requested Turkic troops to cross the river south. Changsun forged an edict to Mohuaduo She to thwart their plot. A Tang envoy also arrived at the same time, and the Turkic troops did not march south.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，詔右武候驃騎將軍高世靜聘始畢可汗，至豐州而始畢死，詔留金幣不遣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude an edict sent Right Martial Guard Cavalry General Gao Shijing as envoy to Shibi Khagan. Reaching Feng Prefecture, Shibi died, and an edict ordered the gold and silk retained and not sent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude an edict sent Right Martial Guard Cavalry General Gao Shijing as envoy to Shibi Khagan. Reaching Feng Prefecture, he learned that Shibi had died, and an edict ordered that the gold and silk be retained and not sent.

sentences.zh: 突厥怒，引兵南至河。

translations.literal: The Turks were angry and led troops south to the river.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were enraged and led troops south to the river.

sentences.zh: 長遜遣世靜出塞勞之，且若專致賻賜者，虜引還。

translations.literal: Changsun sent Shijing beyond the frontier to comfort them and, as if specially delivering condolence gifts, the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun sent Shijing beyond the frontier to greet them and, as if specially delivering condolence gifts, persuaded the Turks to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 授總管，改楊國公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commander-in-Chief and his title was changed to Duke of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commander-in-Chief and his title was changed to Duke of Yang.

sentences.zh: 及討薛舉，不待命輒引兵會，賜錦袍金甲。

translations.literal: When campaigning against Xue Ju, without awaiting orders he led troops to join the force and was granted a brocade robe and golden armor.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Xue Ju began, he led troops to join the force without awaiting orders and was granted a brocade robe and golden armor.

sentences.zh: 或譖長遜居豐久，恐與突厥為脣齒，乃請入朝，授右武候將軍，徙息國公，加賜宮人、彩千段。

translations.literal: Some slandered Changsun for dwelling at Feng long, fearing he and the Turks had become lip and teeth; he therefore requested to enter court, was appointed Right Martial Guard General, his title moved to Duke of Xi, and palace women and a thousand bolts of colored silk were additionally granted.
translations.idiomatic: Some slandered Changsun for having long resided at Feng, fearing he and the Turks had become mutually dependent like lip and teeth. He therefore requested to enter court, was appointed Right Martial Guard General, had his title changed to Duke of Xi, and was additionally granted palace women and a thousand bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 屬有疾，高祖親問之。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, Gaozu personally inquired after him.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, Gaozu personally inquired after him.

sentences.zh: 後竇軌率巴、蜀兵擊王世充，以長遜檢校益州行臺左僕射。

translations.literal: Later Dou Gui led Ba and Shu troops against Wang Shichong, and Changsun was appointed acting Left Vice Director of the Yizhou Executive Office.
translations.idiomatic: Later Dou Gui led Ba and Shu troops against Wang Shichong, and Changsun was appointed acting Left Vice Director of the Yizhou Executive Office.

sentences.zh: 歷遂、夔二總管，政以惠稱。

translations.literal: He passed through the two commanderships of Sui and Kui, and his governance was known for kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commander-in-chief of Sui and Kui in succession, and his governance was known for its kindness.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十一年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the eleventh year of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year of the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 張平高，綏州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Pinggao was a native of Sui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pinggao was a native of Sui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為隋鷹揚府校尉，戍太原，遂預謀議。

translations.literal: He was a captain of a Sui hawkish garrison, garrisoned at Taiyuan, and thus took part in the deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: He was a captain of a Sui hawkish garrison, garrisoned at Taiyuan, and thus took part in the early deliberations.

sentences.zh: 從唐公平京城，累授左領軍將軍，封蕭國公。

translations.literal: He followed the Duke of Tang in pacifying the capital region and was repeatedly appointed Left Leading Guard General and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Duke of Tang in pacifying the capital region, was repeatedly promoted to Left Leading Guard General, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，為丹州刺史，坐事，以右光祿大夫還第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he became governor of Dan Prefecture. Convicted of an offense, he returned home as Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he became governor of Dan Prefecture. Convicted of an offense, he was sent home with the title Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒，追封羅國，贈潭州都督。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Luo and granted Protector-General of Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Luo and made Protector-General of Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李安遠，夏州人。

translations.literal: Li Anyuan was a native of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Anyuan was a native of Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父徹，隋上柱國、雲州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Che was a Sui Senior Pillar of State and governor of Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Che was a Sui Senior Pillar of State and governor of Yun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世為將家，以財雄。

translations.literal: For generations they were a military family, powerful through wealth.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they were a military family, powerful through wealth.

sentences.zh: 安遠少無檢，與博徙遊，至破產。

translations.literal: Anyuan in youth lacked restraint; he gambled and wandered until he was bankrupt.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Anyuan was unrestrained; he gambled and drifted until he had ruined himself.

sentences.zh: 晚乃折節向書，從士大夫，茍勝己，必傾心交之。

translations.literal: Only later did he restrain himself and turn to books; he followed scholar-officials, and if anyone surpassed himself he would devote his heart and befriend them.
translations.idiomatic: Only later did he reform his ways and turn to books. He sought out scholar-officials, and whenever he met someone better than himself, he would wholeheartedly befriend them.

sentences.zh: 襲爵城陽公。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Duke of Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title of Duke of Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 與王珪最善，珪坐王頗得罪，當流，安遠為營護免。

translations.literal: He was closest with Wang Gui; Gui was convicted on account of Wang Pi and should have been exiled; Anyuan made arrangements to protect and free him.
translations.idiomatic: He was on closest terms with Wang Gui. When Gui was convicted on account of Wang Pi and faced exile, Anyuan made arrangements to protect him and secure his release.

sentences.zh: 後補正平令。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed magistrate of Zhengping.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed magistrate of Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 兵起，攻絳州，安遠與通守陳叔達嬰城拒。

translations.literal: When the army rose they attacked Jiang Prefecture; Anyuan and Administrator Chen Shuda held the city in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the army rose they attacked Jiang Prefecture. Anyuan and the administrator Chen Shuda held the city and resisted.

sentences.zh: 唐公素與安遠善，及拔絳，撫慰其家，引與同食，授右翊衛統軍、正平縣公。

translations.literal: The Duke of Tang had long been on good terms with Anyuan; when Jiang fell he comforted his family, brought him to eat together, and granted Right Yiling Guard Commander and Duke of Zhengping County.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Tang had long been on good terms with Anyuan. When Jiang fell he comforted Anyuan's family, invited him to eat with him, and appointed him Right Yiling Guard Commander and Duke of Zhengping County.

sentences.zh: 後從破屈突通，進上柱國、右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he followed in defeating Qu Tu Tong and was advanced to Senior Pillar of State and Right Martial Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Later he took part in defeating Qu Tu Tong and was promoted to Senior Pillar of State and Right Martial Guard Grand General.

sentences.zh: 數從秦王征討，積功，累封至廣德郡公。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he followed the Prince of Qin in campaigns; merit accumulated, and through repeated enfeoffments he reached Duke of Guangde Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly followed the Prince of Qin on campaign, accumulated merit, and through successive enfeoffments rose to Duke of Guangde Commandery.

sentences.zh: 奉使吐谷渾，安遠與約和，吐谷渾乃請為互市，邊場利之。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to Tuyuhun, Anyuan made peace with them; Tuyuhun then requested mutual markets, and the frontier benefited.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Tuyuhun, Anyuan negotiated peace with them. Tuyuhun then requested mutual trade markets, to the benefit of the frontier.

sentences.zh: 隱太子將亂，陰使誘動，安遠介無貳誌，秦王益親重。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Crown Prince was about to rebel, secret envoys tried to entice and stir him; Anyuan's integrity had no divided will; the Prince of Qin grew ever closer and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hidden Crown Prince was about to rebel, secret envoys tried to win him over, but Anyuan's loyalty never wavered. The Prince of Qin grew all the more close to him and held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，嘗命統邏騎都下，督盜賊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was once ordered to command patrol cavalry in the capital and supervise against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he was once ordered to command patrol cavalry in the capital and suppress banditry.

sentences.zh: 歷潞州都督、懷州刺史，皆以幹用顯，然急刻少恩，由是損名。

translations.literal: He passed through Protector-General of Lu Prefecture and governor of Huai Prefecture; in all he distinguished himself by practical ability, yet was harsh and sparing in kindness, and thereby his reputation suffered.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Protector-General of Lu Prefecture and governor of Huai Prefecture in succession, distinguishing himself by practical ability in both posts, yet he was harsh and unforgiving, and thereby his reputation suffered.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈涼州都督，謚曰安，追封遂安郡公。

translations.literal: He died, was posthumously granted Protector-General of Liang Prefecture, posthumous name An, and retroactively enfeoffed as Duke of Sui'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Protector-General of Liang Prefecture, given the posthumous name An, and retroactively enfeoffed as Duke of Sui'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 馬三寶，性敏獪。

translations.literal: Ma Sanbao—his nature was quick and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sanbao was quick-witted and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 事柴紹，為家僮。

translations.literal: He served Chai Shao as a household slave.
translations.idiomatic: He served Chai Shao as a household slave.

sentences.zh: 紹尚平陽公主，高祖兵起，紹間道走太原。

translations.literal: Shao married Princess Pingyang; when Gaozu's army rose, Shao took a hidden route and fled to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had married Princess Pingyang. When Gaozu's army rose, Shao took a hidden route and fled to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 三寶奉公主遁司竹園，說賊何潘仁與連和。

translations.literal: Sanbao escorted the princess in flight to Sizhu Garden and persuaded the bandit He Panren to join in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Sanbao escorted the princess in flight to Sizhu Garden and persuaded the bandit leader He Panren to ally with them.

sentences.zh: 潘仁入謁，以百兵為主衛。

translations.literal: Panren entered to pay homage, and a hundred soldiers were assigned as the princess's guard.
translations.idiomatic: Panren came to pay homage, and a hundred soldiers were assigned as the princess's guard.

sentences.zh: 三寶自稱總管，撫接群盜，兵至數萬。

translations.literal: Sanbao styled himself commander-in-chief, pacified and gathered the bandits, and troops reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Sanbao styled himself commander-in-chief, won over the bandits, and raised an army of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 唐公濟河，授三寶左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Tang crossed the river, he granted Sanbao Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Tang crossed the river, he appointed Sanbao Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 秦王至竹林宮，三寶以兵詣軍門謁，遂從平京師，拜太子監門率。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin reached Zhulin Palace, Sanbao brought troops to the army gate to pay homage; he then followed in pacifying the capital and was appointed Crown Prince's Gate Guard Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin reached Zhulin Palace, Sanbao brought his troops to the army gate to pay homage. He then took part in pacifying the capital and was appointed Crown Prince's Gate Guard Commander.

sentences.zh: 別擊叛胡劉拔真於北山，破之。

translations.literal: Separately he struck the rebellious Hu Liu Bazhen at North Mountain and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He separately attacked the rebellious Hu leader Liu Bazhen at North Mountain and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 從平薛仁杲。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Xue Rengao.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in pacifying Xue Rengao.

sentences.zh: 與柴紹擊吐谷渾於岷州，先鋒陷陣，斬名王，俘執數千，以功封新興縣男。

translations.literal: With Chai Shao he attacked Tuyuhun at Min Prefecture; as vanguard he broke the formation, beheaded a famous king, captured several thousand, and for merit was enfeoffed as Baron of Xinxing County.
translations.idiomatic: With Chai Shao he attacked Tuyuhun at Min Prefecture. Leading the vanguard he broke the enemy lines, beheaded a prominent king, and took several thousand prisoners. For his merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xinxing County.

sentences.zh: 後高祖幸司竹園，顧謂曰：「汝興兵處邪？

translations.literal: Later when Gaozu visited Sizhu Garden, he turned and said: "Is this where you raised troops?
translations.idiomatic: Later when Gaozu visited Sizhu Garden, he turned to him and said, "Is this where you raised your army?

sentences.zh: 衛青大不惡。

translations.literal: Wei Qing was hardly bad.
translations.idiomatic: Not bad at all—like Wei Qing!

sentences.zh: 」貞觀初，拜左驍衛大將軍，進爵為公，卒謚曰忠。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Zhenguan he was appointed Left Xiao Guard Grand General, advanced in rank to duke, and upon death received posthumous name Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: " At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he was appointed Left Xiao Guard Grand General, promoted to duke, and upon death was given the posthumous name Zhong.

sentences.zh: 李孟嘗，趙州人。

translations.literal: Li Mengchang was a native of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mengchang was a native of Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 終右威衛大將軍、漢東郡公。

translations.literal: He ended as Right Majestic Guard Grand General and Duke of Handong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Right Majestic Guard Grand General and Duke of Handong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 元仲文，洛州人。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhongwen was a native of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhongwen was a native of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 終右監門將軍、河南縣公。

translations.literal: He ended as Right Gate Guard General and Duke of Henan County.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Right Gate Guard General and Duke of Henan County.

sentences.zh: 秦行師，并州人。

translations.literal: Qin Xingshi was a native of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xingshi was a native of Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 終右監門將軍、清水郡公。

translations.literal: He ended as Right Gate Guard General and Duke of Qingshui Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Right Gate Guard General and Duke of Qingshui Commandery.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：應龍之翔，雲霧滃然而從，震風薄怒，萬空不約而號，物有自然相動耳。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: When the responding dragon soars, clouds and mist billow and follow; thunder-wind presses near in anger, the ten thousand hollows without appointment cry out—things have their natural mutual stirring, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal reads: When the responding dragon soars, clouds and mist surge to follow; when thunder-winds press close in fury, every hollow cries out unbidden—things stir one another by nature, that is all.

sentences.zh: 觀二子非有踔越之姿，當高祖受命，赫然利見於世，故能或翼或從，屍天之功雲。

translations.literal: Observing the two men—they had no transcendent mien—yet when Gaozu received the Mandate, splendidly they appeared to advantage in the world, and so were able sometimes to wing, sometimes to follow, sharing Heaven's merit as clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Consider these two men: they had no extraordinary brilliance. Yet when Gaozu received the Mandate and shone forth upon the world, they were able to wing or follow as needed and share in Heaven's achievement like clouds in the dragon's train.

sentences.zh: 文靜數履軍陷陣，以才自進，而寂專用串昵顯。

translations.literal: Wenjing repeatedly marched with the army and broke formations, advancing through his own talent, while Ji relied solely on close intimacy to shine.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing repeatedly took the field and broke enemy lines, rising through his own talent, while Ji rose solely through close personal ties to the ruler.

sentences.zh: 外者易乘，邇者難疏，故文靜先被躁望誅，寂後坐訞言斥，誠異夫蕭何、曹參雲！

translations.literal: Those at a distance are easy to mount against; those nearby are hard to keep at arm's length—hence Wenjing was first put to death on restless ambition, while Ji later was expelled on delusive words; truly unlike Xiao He and Cao Can indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Outsiders are easy to attack; those close at hand are hard to dislodge. And so Wenjing was first executed on charges of restless ambition, while Ji was later driven out on the weight of slander—a fate truly unlike that of Xiao He and Cao Can!
